parts.label: a
parts.text: A curve is defined by the parametric equations x = t² + 3t, y = t³ − 2t. Find dy/dx in terms of t.
parts.working:
B1 dx/dt = 2t + 3, dy/dt = 3t² − 2
M1 dy/dx = (dy/dt) ÷ (dx/dt)
A1 (3t² − 2)/(2t + 3)

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the equation of the tangent to the curve at the point where t = 1, giving your answer in the form ax + by + c = 0.
parts.working:
B1 point (4, −1)
B1 gradient 1/5
M1 y + 1 = (1/5)(x − 4)
A1 x − 5y − 9 = 0 (any equivalent integer form)

parts.label: a
parts.text: A curve is defined for t > 0 by x = 1 + ln(2t), y = t² + 2/t. Show that dy/dx = 2t² − 2/t.
parts.working:
B1 dx/dt = 1/t
B1 dy/dt = 2t − 2/t²
A1 divide to obtain the given result

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the exact coordinates of the stationary point of the curve.
parts.working:
M1 2t² − 2/t = 0 so t³ = 1, t = 1
A1 x = 1 + ln 2, y = 3

parts.label: a
parts.text: The parametric equations of a curve are x = e²ᵗ − 1, y = t eᵗ. Show that dy/dx = (1 + t)/(2eᵗ).

M1 divide and cancel eᵗ, A1 given answer

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the exact coordinates of the point on the curve at which the tangent is parallel to the x-axis.

A1 x = e⁻² − 1, y = −e⁻¹

parts.label: c
parts.text: Find the equation of the normal to the curve at the origin.
parts.working:
B1 origin when t = 0, gradient 1/2
A1 normal gradient −2, y = −2x

parts.label: a
parts.text: A curve has parametric equations x = 4 sin θ, y = 3 cos 2θ, for −½π < θ < ½π. Show that dy/dx = −3 sin θ.
parts.answer: dy/dx = −6 sin 2θ ÷ 4 cos θ = −12 sin θ cos θ ÷ 4 cos θ = −3 sin θ
parts.working:
B1 dx/dθ = 4 cos θ, B1 dy/dθ = −6 sin 2θ
M1 use sin 2θ = 2 sin θ cos θ and simplify to the given answer

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the equation of the tangent to the curve at the point where θ = π/6, giving your answer in the form ax + by = c where a, b and c are integers.
parts.working:
B1 point (2, 3/2) and gradient −3/2
M1 y − 3/2 = −3/2(x − 2)
A1 3x + 2y = 9

parts.label: c
parts.text: Find the Cartesian equation of the curve in the form y = f(x).

parts.label: a
parts.text: A spiral curve is given by x = eᵗ cos t, y = eᵗ sin t, for 0 ≤ t ≤ π. Show that dy/dx = (sin t + cos t)/(cos t − sin t).
parts.answer: dx/dt = eᵗ(cos t − sin t), dy/dt = eᵗ(sin t + cos t); divide
parts.working:
B1 both derivatives by the product rule
M1 divide and cancel eᵗ
A1 given answer

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the exact coordinates of the point on the curve where the tangent is parallel to the y-axis.
parts.working:

parts.label: c
parts.text: Find the exact value of t at which the tangent is parallel to the x-axis, and find the equation of the tangent at the point where t = 0.
parts.answer: t = 3π/4; tangent at t = 0: y = x − 1
parts.working:

B1 point (1, 0), gradient 1
B1 y = x − 1

parts.label: a
parts.text: The equation of a curve is x² + 3xy + 2y² = 6. Show that the point (1, 1) lies on the curve and find dy/dx in terms of x and y.
parts.working:

A1 dy/dx = −(2x + 3y)/(3x + 4y)

parts.label: b

parts.label: a
parts.text: A curve has equation y³ + x²y − 2x = 8. Find dy/dx in terms of x and y.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The equation of a curve is 2x² − xy + y² = 28. Show that dy/dx = (y − 4x)/(2y − x).
parts.answer: 4x − y − x dy/dx + 2y dy/dx = 0, so dy/dx = (y − 4x)/(2y − x)

M1 implicit differentiation including product rule on xy
A1 4x − (y + x dy/dx) + 2y dy/dx = 0

parts.label: b

parts.label: a
parts.text: The curve y = sin x/(2 + cos x) is defined for 0 ≤ x ≤ 2π. Show that dy/dx = (2 cos x + 1)/(2 + cos x)².
parts.answer: Quotient rule: [cos x(2 + cos x) + sin²x]/(2 + cos x)² = (2 cos x + 1)/(2 + cos x)²
parts.working:
M1 quotient rule
A1 numerator 2 cos x + cos²x + sin²x
A1 use cos²x + sin²x = 1 for the given answer

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the exact coordinates of the stationary points and state which is the maximum.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The curve C has equation y = (2x − 1)/√(x² + 2). Show that dy/dx = (x + 4)/(x² + 2)^(3/2).

A1 correct unsimplified derivative
M1 multiply through by (x² + 2)^(½)

parts.answer: y → 2 as x → ∞ and y → −2 as x → −∞; range −3/√2 ≤ y < 2
parts.working:
B1 both limits
B1 range −3√2/2 ≤ y < 2

parts.label: a

parts.label: b

parts.label: b

parts.label: a
parts.text: The curve y = sin 2x + 2 cos x is defined for 0 ≤ x ≤ π. Show that dy/dx = −2(2 sin x − 1)(sin x + 1).
parts.answer: dy/dx = 2 cos 2x − 2 sin x = 2(1 − 2 sin²x − sin x) = −2(2 sin x − 1)(sin x + 1)
parts.working:
B1 2 cos 2x − 2 sin x
M1 cos 2x = 1 − 2 sin²x
A1 factorised to the given answer

parts.label: b

parts.label: a
parts.text: Show that, for small values of x, √((1 + x)/(1 − x)) ≈ 1 + x + ½x².
parts.working: (1 + x)^½ = 1 + ½x − ⅛x² B1; (1 − x)^(−½) = 1 + ½x + ⅜x² M1 A1; multiply: 1 + x + (⅜ − ⅛ + ¼)x² M1; = 1 + x + ½x² A1

parts.label: b
parts.text: By substituting x = 1/7, show that √3 ≈ 196/113, and find the percentage error in this approximation, correct to 2 significant figures.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the quotient and remainder when 2x⁴ − 3x³ + x² + 5x − 4 is divided by x² − x + 2.
parts.working: Long division: first term 2x² M1; quotient 2x² − x − 4 A1 A1; remainder 3x + 4 A1

parts.label: a
parts.text: The polynomial x⁴ + 2x³ + ax + b, where a and b are constants, is divided by x² + x − 2. The remainder is 3x + 1. Find the quotient and the values of a and b.
parts.working: Divide: quotient x² + x + 1 M1 A1; remainder (a + 1)x + (b + 2) A1; a + 1 = 3, a = 2 A1; b + 2 = 1, b = −1 A1

parts.label: b
parts.text: Using these values of a and b, find the remainder when the polynomial is divided by (x − 1).

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the quotient and remainder when 2x³ + x² + 4x + 5 is divided by x² + 1.
parts.working: Long division M1; quotient 2x + 1 A1; remainder 2x + 4 A1

parts.label: b
parts.text: Hence find the exact value of the integral of (2x³ + x² + 4x + 5)/(x² + 1) with respect to x from 0 to 1.
parts.working: Integrand = 2x + 1 + 2x/(x² + 1) + 4/(x² + 1) B1; [x² + x] B1; ln(x² + 1) B1; 4 tan⁻¹x B1; = 2 + ln 2 + π A1

parts.label: a
parts.text: A particle moves in a straight line. Its velocity t seconds after leaving a fixed point O is v m s⁻¹, where v = 6t − t² for 0 ≤ t ≤ 6. Find the acceleration of the particle when t = 2.
parts.working: a = dv/dt = 6 − 2t M1; = 2 m s⁻² A1

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the maximum velocity of the particle.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Find the distance travelled by the particle in the 6 seconds.

parts.label: a
parts.text: A particle starts from rest at a point O and moves in a straight line. Its acceleration t seconds later is (4 − 2t) m s⁻². Find an expression for the velocity of the particle in terms of t.
parts.working: v = ∫(4 − 2t) dt = 4t − t² + c M1; v = 0 at t = 0 so c = 0 A1

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the displacement of the particle from O when it next comes to instantaneous rest.

parts.label: a
parts.text: A particle P moves along a straight line so that its displacement from a fixed point O after t seconds is s m, where s = t³ − 9t² + 24t. Find the values of t when P is at instantaneous rest.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the total distance travelled by P in the first 4 seconds.

parts.label: a
parts.text: A car moves between two sets of traffic lights in Karachi. It starts from rest and its velocity t seconds later is v m s⁻¹, where v = 0.3t² − 0.02t³. Show that the car comes to rest again when t = 15.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the maximum speed of the car.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Find the distance between the two sets of traffic lights.

parts.label: a
parts.text: A particle moves in a straight line from rest at O. Its velocity t seconds later is v m s⁻¹, where v = 3√t for 0 ≤ t ≤ 4. Find the acceleration of the particle when t = 1.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the distance travelled by the particle in the 4 seconds.

parts.label: a
parts.text: A particle starts from rest at O and moves in a straight line. For 0 ≤ t ≤ 4 its velocity is v = 1.5t² − 0.25t³ m s⁻¹. For t ≥ 4 it decelerates uniformly, its velocity being v = 24 − 4t, until it comes to rest. Find the maximum acceleration of the particle for 0 ≤ t ≤ 4.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Show that the velocity is continuous at t = 4 and find the time at which the particle comes to rest.
parts.answer: v(4) = 8 in both; rest at t = 6

parts.label: c
parts.text: Find the total distance travelled by the particle.
parts.working: ∫₀⁴(1.5t² − 0.25t³) dt = [0.5t³ − t⁴/16] M1; = 32 − 16 = 16 A1; second stage ½ × 2 × 8 = 8 M1; total 24 m A1

parts.label: a
parts.text: A particle moves in a straight line, starting at O. Its velocity after t seconds is v m s⁻¹, where v = t² − 7t + 10. Find the times at which the particle changes its direction of motion.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the total distance travelled by the particle in the interval 0 ≤ t ≤ 6.

parts.label: a
parts.text: A particle leaves a point O with velocity 9 m s⁻¹ and moves in a straight line. Its acceleration t seconds later is (6t − 12) m s⁻². Find an expression for the velocity of the particle and its minimum velocity.
parts.working: v = 3t² − 12t + c M1; c = 9 A1; minimum when a = 0, t = 2 M1; v = 12 − 24 + 9 = −3 m s⁻¹ A1

parts.label: b
parts.text: Show that the particle returns to O when t = 3, and find the total distance it has travelled by then.

parts.label: a
parts.text: A train travels between two stations. Its velocity t seconds after leaving the first station is v m s⁻¹, where v = kt(100 − t) and k is a constant; it stops at the second station when t = 100. The distance between the stations is 2500 m. Find k.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the maximum speed of the train.
parts.working: Maximum at t = 50 M1; v = 0.015 × 50 × 50 = 37.5 m s⁻¹ A1

parts.label: a
parts.text: A particle starts from rest at a point O and moves in a straight line. Its velocity t seconds later is v m s⁻¹, where v = 4 − 16/(t + 2)². Find the initial acceleration of the particle.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the displacement of the particle from O when t = 6.

parts.label: c
parts.text: State the value that the velocity approaches as t becomes large.

parts.label: a
parts.text: A lift in a tall building in Dubai starts from rest and moves upwards. For 0 ≤ t ≤ 2 its velocity is v = t − 0.25t² m s⁻¹. Find the velocity and the acceleration of the lift when t = 2.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the distance travelled by the lift in the first 2 seconds.

parts.label: c
parts.text: The lift then moves at constant speed 1 m s⁻¹ and finally slows down to rest, the final stage taking 2 seconds and covering 4/3 m. The lift rises 30 m in total. Find the total time of the journey.
parts.working: Constant-speed distance = 30 − 8/3 = 82/3 m M1; time at constant speed = 82/3 s A1; total = 4 + 82/3 = 94/3 s A1

parts.label: a
parts.text: A cyclist P passes a point O at time t = 0 and continues along a straight road at a constant speed of 9 m s⁻¹. Two seconds later a motorcyclist Q starts from rest at O and follows P along the same road. The velocity of Q is (t − 2)² m s⁻¹ for t ≥ 2, where t is the time in seconds after P passed O. Writing τ = t − 2, show that Q catches up with P when τ³ − 27τ − 54 = 0.
parts.working: Displacement of Q = ∫(t − 2)² dt = (t − 2)³/3 = τ³/3 M1 A1; P: 9t = 9(τ + 2); τ³/3 = 9τ + 18 ⇒ τ³ − 27τ − 54 = 0 A1

parts.label: b
parts.text: Hence find the time at which Q catches up with P, the distance from O at that moment, and the speed of Q at that moment.
parts.answer: t = 8 s; 72 m from O; Q's speed 36 m s⁻¹
parts.working: (τ − 6)(τ + 3)² = 0 M1; τ = 6, so t = 8 s A1; distance = 9 × 8 = 72 m A1; v_Q = 6² = 36 m s⁻¹ A1

parts.label: a
parts.text: A particle starts from rest at O and moves in a straight line. Its velocity, in m s⁻¹, at time t s is v = 6t − 1.5t² for 0 ≤ t ≤ 4 and v = −0.5(t − 4)(10 − t) for 4 ≤ t ≤ 10. Find the greatest speed of the particle during the 10 seconds.
parts.working: First stage: 6 − 3t = 0, t = 2, v = 6 M1 A1; second stage: minimum at t = 7, v = −4.5, speed 4.5 M1; greatest speed 6 m s⁻¹ A1

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the total distance travelled by the particle and its final distance from O.
parts.answer: Total distance 34 m; finally 2 m from O (on the opposite side of O)
parts.working: ∫₀⁴ = [3t² − 0.5t³] = 16 M1 A1; ∫₄¹⁰ −0.5(t − 4)(10 − t) dt = −18 M1 A1; distance 16 + 18 = 34 m, displacement −2, so 2 m from O A1

parts.label: a
parts.text: A particle moves in a straight line. Its velocity at time t s is v = pt² + qt + r m s⁻¹, where p, q and r are constants. Initially its velocity is 5 m s⁻¹ and its acceleration is −6 m s⁻². It is at instantaneous rest when t = 1. Find p, q and r.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the distance between the two positions where the particle is at instantaneous rest.
parts.working: (t − 1)(t − 5) = 0, second rest at t = 5 B1; s = t³/3 − 3t² + 5t M1; s(1) = 7/3, s(5) = −25/3 A1; distance 32/3 m A1

parts.label: a
parts.text: A particle moves in a straight line from rest at O. Its velocity after t seconds is v = 4√t − t m s⁻¹ for 0 ≤ t ≤ 16. Find the maximum velocity of the particle.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the time at which the acceleration of the particle is 0.5 m s⁻².

parts.label: c
parts.text: Show that the particle is at rest when t = 16, and find its distance from O at that time.

parts.label: a
parts.text: A particle P moves in a straight line, starting from a point O. Its displacement from O after t seconds is s = t³ − 12t metres. Find the total distance travelled by P in the first 4 seconds.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the exact time at which P returns to O, and its acceleration at that moment, correct to 3 significant figures.

parts.label: a
parts.text: A metro train starts from rest at a station and accelerates uniformly to a speed of 12 m s⁻¹ in 8 s. It travels at this speed for 20 s and then decelerates uniformly to rest at the next station in 6 s. Sketch the velocity-time graph for the journey.
parts.answer: Trapezium: (0, 0) to (8, 12), horizontal to (28, 12), down to (34, 0)
parts.working: Correct shape B1; values 8, 28, 34 and 12 marked B1

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the distance between the two stations.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Find the average speed of the train for the journey, correct to 3 significant figures.

parts.label: a
parts.text: A girl walks from her home to a shop and back. Her displacement–time graph consists of straight line segments joining the points (0, 0), (10, 50), (25, 50) and (40, 0), where time is in seconds and displacement from home is in metres. Find her velocity in each of the three stages.
parts.answer: 5 m s⁻¹, 0 m s⁻¹, −10/3 m s⁻¹

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find her average speed and her average velocity for the whole 40 seconds.
parts.answer: Average speed 2.5 m s⁻¹; average velocity 0
parts.working: 100/40 = 2.5 B1; displacement 0 so average velocity 0 B1

parts.label: a
parts.text: A car starts from rest and accelerates uniformly to a speed of V m s⁻¹ in 10 s. It then travels at V m s⁻¹ for 40 s before decelerating uniformly to rest in 6 s. The total distance travelled is 1260 m. Use a velocity-time graph to find V.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the deceleration of the car.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Car A passes a point X at a constant speed of 20 m s⁻¹. At the same instant car B starts from rest at X and accelerates uniformly at 2.5 m s⁻² until it reaches 30 m s⁻¹, after which it travels at constant speed. Both cars travel along the same straight road. Sketch on the same axes the velocity-time graphs for the two cars.
parts.answer: A: horizontal line v = 20; B: line from (0, 0) to (12, 30) then horizontal at 30
parts.working: A correct B1; B correct with t = 12 shown B1

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the time at which car B overtakes car A and the distance from X at that time.
parts.working: B reaches 30 m s⁻¹ at t = 12, having travelled 180 m (A has travelled 240 m) M1 A1; 180 + 30(t − 12) = 20t M1; t = 18 s, distance 360 m A1

parts.label: a
parts.text: A particle moves in a straight line, starting at O. Its velocity-time graph consists of straight line segments joining (0, 10), (8, −6), (12, −6) and (15, 0), where t is in seconds and v in m s⁻¹. Find the time at which the particle is instantaneously at rest for the first time, and the total distance travelled in the 15 seconds.
parts.working: Gradient −2, so v = 0 at t = 5 B1; area above axis ½ × 5 × 10 = 25 B1; area below: ½ × 3 × 6 + 4 × 6 + ½ × 3 × 6 = 42 M1; total 67 m A1

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the time at which the particle passes back through O, and its final displacement from O.
parts.answer: t = 32/3 s (10.7 s); 17 m on the negative side of O
parts.working: Need 25 m below the axis: 9 m by t = 8, then 16 m more at 6 m s⁻¹ M1; t = 8 + 16/6 = 32/3 s A1; final displacement 25 − 42 = −17 m A1

parts.label: a
parts.text: A bus starts from rest at one stop and accelerates uniformly at a m s⁻² until its speed is 15 m s⁻¹. It travels at 15 m s⁻¹ and then decelerates uniformly at 2a m s⁻² to rest at the next stop. The journey takes 120 s and the distance between the stops is 1575 m. Show that the total time spent accelerating and decelerating is 22.5/a seconds.
parts.working: Accelerating time 15/a B1; decelerating time 15/(2a) = 7.5/a B1

parts.label: b
parts.text: Use a velocity-time graph to find a.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Take g = 10 m s⁻². A ball is thrown vertically upwards from ground level with speed 14 m s⁻¹. Find the greatest height reached by the ball.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the time taken for the ball to return to the ground.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Find the length of time for which the ball is more than 5 m above the ground, correct to 3 significant figures.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Take g = 10 m s⁻². A stone is thrown vertically upwards with speed 8 m s⁻¹ from a point at the top of a vertical sea cliff, 40 m above the sea. Find the time taken for the stone to reach the sea, correct to 3 significant figures.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the speed with which the stone hits the sea, correct to 3 significant figures.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Take g = 10 m s⁻². A particle A is projected vertically upwards from a point O with speed 20 m s⁻¹. One second later a particle B is projected vertically upwards from O with speed 25 m s⁻¹. Find the time after A is projected at which the two particles are at the same height.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find this height and the velocity of each particle at that moment.
parts.answer: 20 m; A at rest (0 m s⁻¹), B moving upwards at 15 m s⁻¹

parts.label: a
parts.text: Take g = 10 m s⁻². A ball P is released from rest at the top of a building 45 m high. At the same instant a ball Q is thrown vertically upwards with speed 18 m s⁻¹ from the ground directly below. Show that the balls meet 2.5 s later, and find their height above the ground when they meet.
parts.working: Distance fallen by P = 5t², height of Q = 18t − 5t² M1; 5t² + 18t − 5t² = 45 M1; t = 2.5 A1; height = 45 − 5(2.5)² = 13.75 m A1

parts.label: b
parts.text: Show that Q is moving downwards when the balls meet, and find the speed of each ball at that moment.
parts.answer: v_Q = −7 m s⁻¹ (downwards, speed 7); P speed 25 m s⁻¹
parts.working: Q reaches its highest point at t = 1.8 s < 2.5 s, so it is moving down B1; v_Q = 18 − 25 = −7, speed 7 m s⁻¹ B1; v_P = 10 × 2.5 = 25 m s⁻¹ B1

parts.label: a
parts.text: A car slows down uniformly from 25 m s⁻¹ to 10 m s⁻¹ while travelling 105 m along a straight road. Find the deceleration of the car.
parts.working: 10² = 25² + 2a(105) M1; a = −2.5, deceleration 2.5 m s⁻² A1

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the time taken.

parts.label: a
parts.text: A cyclist passes a point A at 4 m s⁻¹ and accelerates uniformly at 0.8 m s⁻² for 10 s. Find her speed at the end of the 10 s and the distance travelled in that time.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the distance she travels during the tenth second.

parts.label: a
parts.text: A particle moves along a straight line with constant acceleration. It passes point A, then point B 3 s later, then point C a further 2 s later. AB = 24 m and BC = 26 m. Find the acceleration of the particle and its speed at A.
parts.answer: a = 2 m s⁻²; u = 5 m s⁻¹
parts.working: A to B: 24 = 3u + 4.5a M1 A1; A to C: 50 = 5u + 12.5a M1; solving: a = 2 A1, u = 5 A1

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the speed of the particle at C.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Car P passes a point O travelling at 30 m s⁻¹ and immediately decelerates uniformly at 1.5 m s⁻² until it stops. Car Q passes O 4 s after P, travelling at a constant 18 m s⁻¹ in the same direction along the same straight road. Find the time taken for P to stop and the distance from O at which it stops.

parts.label: b
parts.text: A student writes 30t − 0.75t² = 18(t − 4) to find when Q reaches P. Explain why this equation does not give the correct answer.
parts.answer: Its positive root is t ≈ 20.6 s > 20 s, but P has already stopped at t = 20, so the formula for P's displacement no longer applies
parts.working: Solves t² − 16t − 96 = 0, t = 8 + 4√10 ≈ 20.6 M1; this is after P stops at t = 20, so the equation is invalid A1

parts.label: c
parts.text: Find the time, measured from when P passes O, at which Q reaches P.

parts.label: a
parts.text: A rice mill in Sindh fills bags with a nominal mass of 5 kg. The masses are normally distributed with standard deviation 0.08 kg. An inspector suspects that the mean mass is less than 5 kg. A random sample of 20 bags has mean mass 4.962 kg. Test at the 5% significance level whether the inspector's suspicion is justified.
parts.answer: z = −2.12 < −1.645, so reject H₀: there is evidence that the mean mass is less than 5 kg.
parts.working: B1 H₀: μ = 5, H₁: μ < 5; M1 standardise with 0.08/√20; A1 z = −2.12 (or p = 0.0168); M1 compare with −1.645 (or 0.0168 < 0.05); A1 reject H₀, conclusion in context, not over-assertive.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The heights of seedlings of a certain plant after 4 weeks are normally distributed with mean 12.4 cm and standard deviation 1.8 cm. A gardener uses a new fertiliser on 40 randomly chosen seedlings and their mean height after 4 weeks is 12.95 cm. Assuming the standard deviation is unchanged, test at the 5% significance level whether the fertiliser increases the mean height.
parts.answer: z = 1.93 > 1.645, so reject H₀: evidence that the mean height has increased.
parts.working: B1 H₀: μ = 12.4, H₁: μ > 12.4; M1 (12.95 − 12.4)/(1.8/√40); A1 1.93; M1 compare with 1.645; A1 conclusion in context.

parts.label: a
parts.text: A health magazine claims that university students sleep 8 hours per night on average. A researcher believes the true mean is lower. The number of hours of sleep is normally distributed with standard deviation 1.2 hours. A random sample of 50 students has mean 7.6 hours. Explain why a one-tailed test is appropriate.
parts.answer: The researcher is only looking for evidence that the mean is lower than 8.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Carry out the test at the 5% significance level.
parts.answer: z = −2.36 < −1.645, so reject H₀: evidence that the mean sleep time is less than 8 hours.
parts.working: B1 H₀: μ = 8, H₁: μ < 8; M1 (7.6 − 8)/(1.2/√50); A1 −2.36; M1 compare with −1.645; A1 conclusion in context.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The lifetimes, x hours, of a random sample of 50 batteries of a certain brand were recorded, giving Σx = 1218 and Σx² = 29 900. Calculate unbiased estimates of the population mean and variance.

parts.label: b
parts.text: The manufacturer claims that the mean lifetime is 25 hours. Test at the 2% significance level whether the mean lifetime differs from 25 hours.
parts.answer: z = −2.09; |z| < 2.326, so do not reject H₀: insufficient evidence that the mean lifetime differs from 25 hours.
parts.working: B1 H₀: μ = 25, H₁: μ ≠ 25; M1 standardise using √(4.684/50); A1 z = −2.09; M1 compare with ±2.326 (two-tailed 2%); A1 do not reject H₀, conclusion in context.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Explain why it was not necessary to assume that the lifetimes are normally distributed.
parts.answer: The sample is large, so by the Central Limit Theorem the sample mean is approximately normally distributed.

parts.label: a
parts.text: A food delivery company says its delivery times have mean 30 minutes and standard deviation 6 minutes. After a change of routes, a random sample of 36 deliveries has mean 32.1 minutes. Assuming the standard deviation is unchanged, test at the 1% significance level whether the mean delivery time has increased.
parts.answer: z = 2.1 < 2.326, so do not reject H₀: insufficient evidence at 1% that the mean has increased.
parts.working: B1 H₀: μ = 30, H₁: μ > 30; M1 (32.1 − 30)/(6/√36); A1 z = 2.1; M1 compare with 2.326; A1 conclusion in context.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the p-value of the test and state the smallest significance level, to the nearest 0.1%, at which H₀ would be rejected.
parts.working: M1 1 − Φ(2.1); A1 0.0179, so reject at levels above 1.79%.

parts.label: a
parts.text: A machine fills bottles with mineral water. The volume is normally distributed with mean 500 ml and standard deviation 4 ml when the machine is working correctly. A random sample of 15 bottles has mean volume 498.1 ml. Test at the 10% significance level whether the mean volume has changed.
parts.answer: z = −1.84; |z| > 1.645, so reject H₀: evidence that the mean volume has changed.
parts.working: B1 H₀: μ = 500, H₁: μ ≠ 500; M1 (498.1 − 500)/(4/√15); A1 −1.84; M1 compare with ±1.645 (5% in each tail); A1 reject H₀, in context.

parts.label: b
parts.text: State one assumption about the sample needed for the test to be valid.
parts.answer: The sample is random (the bottles are chosen independently).

parts.label: a
parts.text: The journey time, x minutes, of a bus route in Karachi was recorded for a random sample of 60 journeys, giving Σ(x − 40) = 90 and Σ(x − 40)² = 1505. Find unbiased estimates of the population mean and variance of the journey time.

parts.label: b
parts.text: The bus company states that the mean journey time is 40 minutes. Test at the 1% significance level whether the mean journey time is greater than 40 minutes.
parts.answer: z = 2.41 > 2.326, so reject H₀: evidence that the mean journey time is greater than 40 minutes.
parts.working: B1 H₀: μ = 40, H₁: μ > 40; M1 1.5/√(23.22/60); A1 2.41; M1 compare with 2.326; A1 conclusion in context.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The scores in an aptitude test are normally distributed with mean 60 and standard deviation 4.5. A coaching centre suspects that students from a certain region score lower on average. A random sample of 25 such students is taken. Find the critical region for the sample mean for a test at the 5% significance level.
parts.working: B1 H₀: μ = 60, H₁: μ < 60; M1 60 − 1.645 × 4.5/√25; A1 58.52; B1 critical region stated as x̄ < 58.52.

parts.label: b
parts.text: The sample mean is found to be 58.7. State, with a reason, the conclusion of the test.
parts.answer: 58.7 is not in the critical region, so do not reject H₀: insufficient evidence that students from the region score lower.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The masses of mangoes from an orchard are normally distributed with mean 80 g and standard deviation 10 g. After a new irrigation system is installed, a random sample of n mangoes has mean mass 82.5 g. A test at the 5% significance level of H₀: μ = 80 against H₁: μ > 80 leads to rejection of H₀. Find the least possible value of n.

parts.label: a
parts.text: A test of H₀: μ = 15 against H₁: μ ≠ 15 is carried out on a normal population with standard deviation 2.4. A random sample of size 30 gives a sample mean of 15.82. Find the p-value of the test.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Hence state the set of significance levels, α%, for which H₀ would be rejected.

parts.label: a
parts.text: A factory tests whether the mean breaking strength of its cables has fallen below 400 N, using a 5% significance level. Explain what is meant by a Type I error in this context.
parts.answer: Concluding that the mean breaking strength has fallen below 400 N when in fact it has not.
parts.working: B1 rejecting H₀ when it is true, in context.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Explain what is meant by a Type II error in this context.
parts.answer: Concluding that the mean breaking strength has not fallen when in fact it has fallen below 400 N.
parts.working: B1 not rejecting H₀ when it is false, in context.

parts.label: c
parts.text: State the probability of making a Type I error.
parts.working: B1 equal to the significance level (the test statistic has a continuous distribution).

parts.label: a
parts.text: Sara suspects that a coin is biased towards heads. She tosses it 10 times and will conclude that it is biased if she obtains 8 or more heads. Find the probability of a Type I error.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Sara obtains 6 heads and concludes that the coin is not biased. State which type of error she might have made, giving a reason.
parts.answer: Type II, because she did not reject H₀ (H₀ could be false).

parts.label: a
parts.text: The reaction times of drivers are normally distributed with mean 100 ms and standard deviation 10 ms. A researcher tests H₀: μ = 100 against H₁: μ > 100 using a sample of 25 drivers who have been awake for 20 hours, and rejects H₀ if the sample mean exceeds 103.29 ms. Find the probability of a Type I error.

parts.label: b
parts.text: The sample mean is 104.1 ms. State the conclusion of the test and the type of error that could have been made.
parts.answer: Reject H₀ (104.1 > 103.29): evidence of a longer mean reaction time; a Type I error could have been made.

parts.label: a
parts.text: In the past, 30% of customers at a bakery bought a cake. After the price rises, the owner tests H₀: p = 0.3 against H₁: p < 0.3 using a random sample of 20 customers. He will reject H₀ if 2 or fewer customers buy a cake. Find the probability of a Type I error.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Given that the true proportion is now 0.15, find the probability of a Type II error.

parts.label: a

parts.text: Find the probability that exactly 3 buses arrive in a 30-minute period and at least one of them is from each route.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The point P(4, −3) lies on the curve y = f(x). State the coordinates of the image of P on the curve y = f(x + 2).
parts.working: B1: translation by 2 units in the negative x-direction.

parts.label: b
parts.text: State the coordinates of the image of P on the curve y = 3f(x).
parts.working: B1: stretch parallel to the y-axis, y-coordinate multiplied by 3.

parts.label: c
parts.text: State the coordinates of the image of P on the curve y = f(−x) − 1.
parts.working: B1 x-coordinate −4 (reflection in the y-axis); B1 y-coordinate −4 (translation 1 unit down).

parts.label: a
parts.text: Describe fully the single transformation that maps the curve y = sin x onto the curve y = sin(x/3).
parts.answer: A stretch parallel to the x-axis with scale factor 3 (y-axis invariant).
parts.working: B1 stretch parallel to the x-axis; B1 scale factor 3.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Describe fully the single transformation that maps the curve y = sin x onto the curve y = −sin x.
parts.working: B1 reflection in the x-axis (or y = 0).

parts.label: a
parts.text: The curve y = x² − 4x + 7 is translated by the vector (−1, 3), written as a column vector with x-component −1 and y-component 3. Find the equation of the new curve in the form y = x² + bx + c.
parts.working: M1 replace x by (x + 1): y = (x + 1)² − 4(x + 1) + 7; M1 add 3; A1 y = x² − 2x + 7.

parts.label: b
parts.text: State the coordinates of the minimum point of the new curve.
parts.working: B1: original minimum (2, 3) moves to (1, 6); or complete the square (x − 1)² + 6.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The curve y = x² − 5x is reflected in the x-axis and then translated by the vector (0, 6). Find the equation of the new curve.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the x-coordinates of the points where the new curve meets the x-axis.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The curve y = f(x) is transformed to the curve y = 2f(x − 1) + 3. Describe fully a sequence of transformations that maps y = f(x) onto y = 2f(x − 1) + 3, making clear the order in which they are applied.
parts.answer: Translation by (1, 0); then stretch parallel to the y-axis, scale factor 2; then translation by (0, 3). (Equivalent: stretch in y, factor 2, then translation (1, 3).)
parts.working: B1 translation 1 unit in positive x-direction; B1 stretch parallel to the y-axis, factor 2; B1 translation 3 units in positive y-direction; B1 correct order (the y-translation must come after the stretch).

parts.label: b
parts.text: The point (3, 5) lies on y = f(x). Find the coordinates of its image on y = 2f(x − 1) + 3.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Express 2x² − 12x + 13 in the form a(x − b)² + c, where a, b and c are constants.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Hence describe fully a sequence of two transformations that maps the curve y = x² onto the curve y = 2x² − 12x + 13.
parts.answer: Stretch parallel to the y-axis with scale factor 2, followed by a translation by the vector (3, −5).
parts.working: B1 stretch, parallel to y-axis, factor 2; B1 translation (3, −5); B1 order correct (stretch first). [Translation (3, 0), stretch factor 2, translation (0, −5) also acceptable.]

parts.label: a
parts.text: The function f is defined by f(x) = x² + 2x for x ∈ ℝ. The curve y = f(x) is reflected in the y-axis and then translated by the vector (3, 0). The resulting curve is y = g(x). Find g(x) in the form x² + px + q.
parts.working: M1 reflection gives y = f(−x) = x² − 2x; M1 replace x by (x − 3): (x − 3)² − 2(x − 3); A1 x² − 8x + 15.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the x-coordinates of the points where y = g(x) crosses the x-axis.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Show that √(4x − 8) can be written in the form k√(x − 2), stating the value of k.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Hence describe fully a sequence of two transformations that maps the curve y = √x onto the curve y = √(4x − 8).
parts.answer: Translation by the vector (2, 0) and a stretch parallel to the y-axis with scale factor 2 (in either order).
parts.working: B1 translation (2, 0); B1 stretch parallel to the y-axis; B1 scale factor 2. [Alternative: translation (8, 0) followed by stretch parallel to x-axis, factor ¼.]

parts.label: a
parts.text: The curve y = x³ is transformed by the following sequence: a translation by the vector (2, 0); then a stretch parallel to the y-axis with scale factor ½; then a reflection in the x-axis. Find the equation of the resulting curve.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the coordinates of the point where the resulting curve crosses the y-axis.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Find the image of the point (1, 1) under the same sequence of transformations.
parts.working: B1 (3, 1) after translation, (3, ½) after stretch; B1 (3, −½).

parts.label: a
parts.text: The curve y = f(x) has a maximum point at (6, 10) and crosses the x-axis at (2, 0). The function g is defined by g(x) = 5 − 2f(½x). Find the coordinates of the stationary point on y = g(x) and state whether it is a maximum or a minimum.
parts.working: B1 x = 6 × 2 = 12; B1 y = 5 − 2 × 10 = −15; B1 minimum (the factor −2 reflects the curve in the x-axis).

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the coordinates of the image of (2, 0) on y = g(x).

parts.label: c
parts.text: Describe fully a sequence of transformations that maps y = f(x) onto y = g(x).
parts.answer: Stretch parallel to the x-axis, factor 2; stretch parallel to the y-axis, factor 2; reflection in the x-axis; translation by (0, 5) — the translation applied last.
parts.working: B1 x-stretch factor 2; B1 y-stretch factor 2; B1 reflection in x-axis; B1 translation (0, 5) after the stretch and reflection (the stretch/reflection may be combined as a y-stretch with factor −2).

parts.label: a
parts.text: The function f is defined by f(x) = x² − 6x + 5 for x ∈ ℝ. The curve y = f(x) is mapped onto the curve y = f(x + k) + m by a translation, and the vertex of the new curve is at (−1, 2). Find the values of k and m.
parts.working: M1 complete the square: f(x) = (x − 3)² − 4, vertex (3, −4); A1 k = 4 (3 − k = −1); A1 m = 6 (−4 + m = 2).

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the y-intercept of the new curve.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Determine whether the new curve meets the line y = x + 4, giving a reason.
parts.answer: Yes, at two points: x² + x − 1 = 0 has discriminant 5 > 0.
parts.working: M1 (x + 1)² + 2 = x + 4 gives x² + x − 1 = 0; A1 discriminant 1 + 4 = 5 > 0, so two points of intersection.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The function f is defined by f(x) = 5x − 3 for x ∈ ℝ. Find an expression for f⁻¹(x).

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the value of f⁻¹(12).

parts.label: a
parts.text: The function f is defined by f(x) = (2x + 1)/(x − 3) for x ≠ 3. Find an expression for f⁻¹(x).
parts.working: M1 y(x − 3) = 2x + 1; M1 collect x terms: x(y − 2) = 3y + 1; A1 f⁻¹(x) = (3x + 1)/(x − 2).

parts.label: b
parts.text: Verify your answer by finding f(5) and then f⁻¹ of your result.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The function g is defined by g(x) = 7 − 3x for −2 ≤ x ≤ 4. Find the range of g.
parts.working: M1 g(4) = −5, g(−2) = 13; A1 correct inequality.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find an expression for g⁻¹(x) and state the domain of g⁻¹.
parts.working: M1 x = (7 − y)/3; A1; B1 domain equals the range of g.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The function f is defined by f(x) = x² − 8x + 21 for x ≥ 4. Express f(x) in the form (x − a)² + b.

parts.label: b
parts.text: State the range of f.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Find an expression for f⁻¹(x) and state the domain of f⁻¹.
parts.working: M1 y − 5 = (x − 4)²; A1 x = 4 + √(y − 5) (positive root as x ≥ 4); B1 domain x ≥ 5.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The function f is defined by f(x) = 3 − 2x² for x ≤ 0. Explain why f has an inverse, but the function g(x) = 3 − 2x² for x ∈ ℝ does not.
parts.answer: f is one-one on x ≤ 0 (strictly increasing there); g is not one-one, e.g. g(1) = g(−1) = 1.
parts.working: B1 f is one-one / increasing for x ≤ 0; B1 g is many-one, with a correct example or reference to symmetry about x = 0.

parts.label: b
parts.text: State the range of f.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Find an expression for f⁻¹(x).
parts.working: M1 x² = (3 − y)/2; M1 square root; A1 negative root chosen because the domain of f is x ≤ 0.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The function f is defined by f(x) = 2x² + 12x + 11 for x ≥ k. Express 2x² + 12x + 11 in the form a(x + b)² + c.

parts.label: b
parts.text: State the smallest value of k for which f has an inverse.

parts.label: c
parts.text: For this value of k, find an expression for f⁻¹(x) and state its domain.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The function f is defined by f(x) = 2 + 4/(x − 1) for x > 1. State the range of f.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find an expression for f⁻¹(x).

parts.label: c
parts.text: State the domain and the range of f⁻¹.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The function f is defined by f(x) = x² − 4x + 6 for x ≥ 2. Find an expression for f⁻¹(x) and state its domain.
parts.working: M1 complete the square: (x − 2)² + 2; A1 f⁻¹(x) = 2 + √(x − 2); B1 domain x ≥ 2.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Explain why the solutions of f(x) = f⁻¹(x) are the same as the solutions of f(x) = x for this function.
parts.answer: f is increasing, so the graphs of y = f(x) and y = f⁻¹(x) (reflections of each other in y = x) can only meet on the line y = x.
parts.working: B1 reference to reflection in y = x with f increasing.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Hence solve the equation f(x) = f⁻¹(x).
parts.working: M1 x² − 4x + 6 = x ⇒ x² − 5x + 6 = 0; A1 (x − 2)(x − 3) = 0; A1 x = 2, 3 (both in the domain).

parts.label: a
parts.text: The function f is defined by f(x) = 3 + 2 sin x for −½π ≤ x ≤ ½π. State the range of f.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find an expression for f⁻¹(x).

parts.label: c
parts.text: Find the exact value of f⁻¹(4).

parts.label: d
parts.text: Explain why f would not have an inverse if its domain were changed to 0 ≤ x ≤ π.
parts.answer: On 0 ≤ x ≤ π the function is not one-one, e.g. f(π/6) = f(5π/6) = 4.
parts.working: B1 not one-one with a reason.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The functions f and g are defined by f(x) = 2x − 5 for x ∈ ℝ and g(x) = 1/(x + 1) for x ≠ −1. Find the value of gf(3).

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find an expression for fg(x) as a single fraction.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The functions f and g are defined for x ∈ ℝ by f(x) = 3x + 2 and g(x) = x² − 1. Find expressions for fg(x) and gf(x).

parts.label: b
parts.text: Solve the equation fg(x) = gf(x), giving your answers in exact form.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The functions f and g are defined for x ∈ ℝ by f(x) = x² + 4x and g(x) = 2x − 3. Find and simplify an expression for gf(x).

parts.label: b
parts.text: Solve the equation fg(x) = 12.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The function f is defined by f(x) = (x + 3)/(x − 1) for x ≠ 1. Show that ff(x) = x.
parts.working: M1 substitute: ((x + 3)/(x − 1) + 3) / ((x + 3)/(x − 1) − 1); M1 multiply through by (x − 1): (4x)/(4); A1 = x.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Hence state an expression for f⁻¹(x).

parts.label: a
parts.text: The function f is defined by f(x) = x² − 6x + 10 for x ≥ 3, and g is defined by g(x) = 2x + k for x ≥ 0, where k is a constant. State the range of f and the range of g in terms of k.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the least value of k for which the composite function fg exists.
parts.working: M1 range of g must lie within the domain of f (x ≥ 3); A1 k ≥ 3, least value 3.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Using k = 3, solve the equation fg(x) = 17.
parts.working: M1 fg(x) = (2x + 3 − 3)² + 1 = 4x² + 1; M1 4x² = 16; A1 x = 2 only (x = −2 is outside the domain of g).

parts.label: a
parts.text: The functions f and g are defined for x ∈ ℝ by f(x) = 2x + 1 and g(x) = x² − 2. Find f⁻¹(x) and gf(x).

parts.label: b
parts.text: Solve the equation gf(x) = f⁻¹(x).

parts.label: a
parts.text: The function f is defined by f(x) = 5 − (x − 2)² for 0 ≤ x ≤ 5. Find the range of f.
parts.working: B1 maximum 5 at x = 2; M1 evaluate ends f(0) = 1, f(5) = −4; A1 −4 ≤ f(x) ≤ 5.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Explain why f does not have an inverse.
parts.answer: f is not one-one on 0 ≤ x ≤ 5, e.g. f(1) = f(3) = 4.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The function f is defined by f(x) = 3/(x + 2) for x ≥ 1. Find the range of f.
parts.working: B1 f(1) = 1 and f decreasing; B1 f(x) > 0 (tends to 0).

parts.label: b
parts.text: The function g is defined by g(x) = x² − 1 for x ∈ ℝ. Find an expression for gf(x) and the range of gf.
parts.working: B1 gf(x); M1 use the range of f as the domain of g; A1 −1 < gf(x) ≤ 0.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The function f is defined by f(x) = 4 sin x − 1 for 0 ≤ x ≤ 7π/6. Find the range of f.
parts.working: B1 maximum of sin x is 1 at x = π/2, giving 3; M1 least value of sin x on the domain is sin(7π/6) = −½; A1 −3 ≤ f(x) ≤ 3.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the largest value of a such that f, with domain 0 ≤ x ≤ a, has an inverse.
parts.working: B1 f is increasing up to x = π/2 only.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The function f is defined by f(x) = x² − 6x + c for 1 ≤ x ≤ 7, where c is a constant. The range of f is −4 ≤ f(x) ≤ 12. Find the value of c and verify that the greatest value is 12.
parts.working: M1 minimum at x = 3: c − 9 = −4; A1 c = 5; B1 f(7) = 12 and f(1) = 0 < 12.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Explain why f does not have an inverse, and state the largest domain of the form 3 ≤ x ≤ b, with b ≤ 7, on which it would have one.
parts.answer: f(1) = f(5) = 0, so f is not one-one; on 3 ≤ x ≤ 7 it is one-one (b = 7).
parts.working: B1 not one-one with example; B1 b = 7.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Take g = 10 m s⁻². A particle of mass 0.4 kg is projected with speed 8 m s⁻¹ up a line of greatest slope of a smooth plane inclined at 30° to the horizontal. Use an energy method to find the distance the particle travels up the plane before coming to instantaneous rest.
parts.working: M1 KE lost = PE gained: ½ × 0.4 × 8² = 0.4 × 10 × d sin 30°. A1 12.8 = 2d. A1 d = 6.4 m.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the speed of the particle when it has travelled 4 m up the plane.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Take g = 10 m s⁻². A child of mass 30 kg slides from rest down a playground slide in a park in Islamabad. The slide is 5 m long and its top is 2.5 m vertically above its bottom. The child reaches the bottom with speed 5 m s⁻¹. Find the work done against resistance.
parts.working: B1 PE lost = 30 × 10 × 2.5 = 750 J. B1 KE gained = ½ × 30 × 25 = 375 J. B1 WD against resistance = 375 J.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Assuming the resistance is constant, find its magnitude.

parts.label: a
parts.text: A block of mass 5 kg is pulled from rest across a rough horizontal floor by a horizontal force of 40 N. The frictional force is 25 N. Find the work done by the 40 N force and the work done against friction when the block has moved 6 m.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Use the work-energy principle to find the speed of the block at this point.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Take g = 10 m s⁻². A cyclist and her bicycle have a total mass of 75 kg. She reaches the bottom of a hill, inclined at an angle α to the horizontal where sin α = 0.06, with speed 8 m s⁻¹ and then free-wheels (does not pedal) up the hill. The resistance to motion is a constant 15 N. Find how far up the hill she travels before coming to rest.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Take g = 10 m s⁻². A ball of mass 0.2 kg is thrown vertically downwards with speed 6 m s⁻¹ from the top of a cliff 25 m above the sea at Gwadar. Ignoring air resistance, use an energy method to find the speed with which the ball hits the sea.

parts.label: b
parts.text: In fact the ball does 40 J of work against air resistance. Find the speed with which it hits the sea.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Take g = 10 m s⁻². A car of mass 1200 kg travels 400 m down a straight hill inclined at an angle α, where sin α = 0.05, with its engine switched off. The resistance to motion is a constant 300 N. The speed of the car at the top is 10 m s⁻¹. Find the loss in potential energy and the work done against resistance.
parts.answer: PE loss 240 000 J; WD against resistance 120 000 J

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the speed of the car at the bottom of the hill.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Take g = 10 m s⁻². A particle of mass 2 kg is released from rest on a rough plane inclined at 25° to the horizontal. The coefficient of friction is 0.3. Find the work done against friction as the particle slides 12 m down the plane.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Use an energy method to find the speed of the particle after it has slid 12 m.
parts.working: M1 ½ × 2v² = 2 × 10 × 12 sin 25° − WD. A1 correct values. A1 v = 6.01.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Take g = 10 m s⁻². A crate of mass 25 kg is pulled along a rough horizontal floor in a warehouse by a rope inclined at 20° above the horizontal. The tension in the rope is 80 N and the coefficient of friction is 0.25. Find the normal reaction and the frictional force.

parts.label: b
parts.text: The crate passes a point A with speed 1 m s⁻¹. Use the work-energy principle to find its speed after it has moved a further 15 m.
parts.working: M1 WD by tension = 80 cos 20° × 15; WD against friction = F × 15. M1 ½ × 25(v² − 1) = difference. A1 v = 4.94.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Take g = 10 m s⁻². A crane on a building site in Lahore raises a load of mass 800 kg vertically from rest through a height of 20 m. At the top the load is moving at 2 m s⁻¹. Ignoring resistances, find the work done by the tension in the cable.
parts.working: B1 PE gain 160 000 J. B1 KE gain 1600 J. B1 total 161 600 J.

parts.label: b
parts.text: The lifting took 40 s. Find the average power of the crane.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Take g = 10 m s⁻². A skier of mass 70 kg skis down a straight slope of length 200 m at a resort in Malam Jabba. The bottom of the slope is 40 m vertically below the top. The skier's speed increases from 3 m s⁻¹ at the top to 20 m s⁻¹ at the bottom. Find the work done against resistances.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the average resistance to motion.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Take g = 10 m s⁻². A small block of mass 0.5 kg slides down a smooth curved ramp. It passes the point A with speed 2 m s⁻¹ and reaches the lowest point B, which is 3 m vertically below A. Find the speed of the block at B.

parts.label: b
parts.text: From B the block moves along a rough horizontal surface, where the coefficient of friction is 0.25, and comes to rest at C. Find the distance BC and the work done against friction between B and C.

parts.label: c
parts.text: The block is now replaced at A and projected with speed u m s⁻¹ so that it stops at a point 20 m beyond B. Find u.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Take g = 10 m s⁻². A block of mass 3 kg is projected with speed 12 m s⁻¹ up a line of greatest slope of a rough plane inclined at 30°. The coefficient of friction is 0.2. Using the work-energy principle, find the distance the block travels up the plane before coming to rest.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Show that the block then slides back down, and find its speed when it returns to the point of projection.
parts.answer: tan 30° = 0.577 > 0.2 so it slides back; speed 8.36 m s⁻¹
parts.working: B1 component of weight 15 N > maximum friction 6 cos 30° = 5.20 N. M1 ½ × 3v² = (15 − 5.196)d. A1 correct substitution. A1 v = 8.36.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Take g = 10 m s⁻². A car of mass 1500 kg moves up a straight hill inclined at an angle α to the horizontal, where sin α = 0.1. The engine exerts a constant driving force of 2500 N and the resistance to motion is a constant 1500 N. The car passes point A at 25 m s⁻¹ and later passes point B at 15 m s⁻¹. Use the work-energy principle to find the distance AB.
parts.working: M1 work-energy equation with four terms. A1 ½ × 1500(625 − 225) = 1500 × 10 × 0.1d + 1500d − 2500d. A1 300 000 = 500d. A1 d = 600 m.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the work done by the driving force between A and B and the increase in potential energy.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Take g = 10 m s⁻². Particle A of mass 3 kg lies on a rough horizontal table, where the coefficient of friction is 0.2. It is attached to a light inextensible string which passes over a smooth pulley at the edge of the table to particle B of mass 2 kg, which hangs freely. The system is released from rest. Use an energy method to find the speed of the particles when B has fallen 1.5 m (A has not reached the pulley).
parts.working: B1 PE lost by B = 2 × 10 × 1.5 = 30 J. B1 WD against friction = 0.2 × 30 × 1.5 = 9 J. M1 ½ × (3 + 2)v² = 30 − 9. A1 v² = 8.4. A1 v = 2.90.

parts.label: b
parts.text: At this instant the string breaks. Find how much further A travels along the table.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Take g = 10 m s⁻². A particle of mass 0.5 kg moves up a line of greatest slope of a rough plane inclined at 20° to the horizontal. It passes point A with speed 9 m s⁻¹ and point B, 5 m further up the plane, with speed 4 m s⁻¹. Find the work done against friction between A and B.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the coefficient of friction between the particle and the plane.

parts.label: a
parts.text: A car travels along a straight level motorway at a constant speed of 25 m s⁻¹. The engine is working at 30 kW. Find the resistance to motion.
parts.working: M1 driving force = 30 000 ÷ 25. A1 constant speed so resistance = 1200 N.

parts.label: b
parts.text: The resistance is unchanged. Find the power needed to travel at a constant 20 m s⁻¹ on the same road.

parts.label: a
parts.text: A car of mass 1000 kg moves along a straight level road with its engine working at 20 kW. The resistance to motion is 500 N. Find the acceleration of the car at the instant when its speed is 10 m s⁻¹.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the greatest possible steady speed of the car on this road with the same power and resistance.

parts.label: a
parts.text: A cyclist and her bicycle have total mass 80 kg. On a level road her maximum power is 240 W and the resistance to motion is a constant 20 N. Find her greatest steady speed.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find her acceleration when she is working at 240 W and travelling at 5 m s⁻¹.
parts.working: B1 driving force 48 N. M1 48 − 20 = 80a. A1 0.35.

parts.label: a
parts.text: A train of mass 200 tonnes travels on a straight level track. Its engine has a maximum power of 800 kW and its greatest steady speed is 40 m s⁻¹. Find the resistance to motion, assumed constant.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the acceleration of the train when it is travelling at 20 m s⁻¹ at full power.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Take g = 10 m s⁻². A car of mass 1400 kg travels at a constant speed of 20 m s⁻¹ up a straight hill inclined at angle α, where sin α = 0.08. The resistance to motion is 700 N. Find the power of the car's engine.

parts.label: b
parts.text: At the top of the hill the road becomes level. The power and resistance are unchanged. Find the initial acceleration of the car on the level road.

parts.label: a
parts.text: A car of mass 1500 kg moves on a level road. The resistance to motion is kv newtons, where v m s⁻¹ is the speed and k is a constant. With the engine working at 45 kW, the greatest steady speed is 30 m s⁻¹. Find k.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the acceleration of the car when it is travelling at 20 m s⁻¹ with the engine working at 45 kW.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Take g = 10 m s⁻². A lorry of mass 8000 kg has a maximum power of 120 kW. The resistance to motion is 3000 N. Find the greatest steady speed of the lorry up a hill inclined at angle α to the horizontal, where sin α = 1/40.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the acceleration of the lorry at an instant when it is moving up the hill at 15 m s⁻¹ with the engine at full power.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Take g = 10 m s⁻². A car of mass 1250 kg moves down a straight hill inclined at angle α, where sin α = 0.04. Its engine works at 15 kW and the resistance to motion is 900 N. Find the acceleration of the car when its speed is 20 m s⁻¹.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the greatest steady speed of the car down the hill with the same power and resistance.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Take g = 10 m s⁻². A minibus of mass 1100 kg travels at a constant speed of 18 m s⁻¹ up a straight road which rises 1 m for every 25 m travelled along the road. The resistance to motion is 450 N. Find the power of the engine.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the work done by the engine while the minibus travels 500 m along the road.

parts.label: a
parts.text: A car of mass 1200 kg tows a trailer of mass 400 kg along a straight level road using a light rigid tow-bar. The resistances to motion are 400 N on the car and 200 N on the trailer. The car's engine works at 24 kW. Find the acceleration when the speed is 15 m s⁻¹.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the tension in the tow-bar at this instant.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Find the greatest steady speed of the car and trailer on this road with the same power.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Take g = 10 m s⁻². A car of mass 1000 kg has a constant power P W and experiences a constant resistance R N. Its greatest steady speed up a hill inclined at angle α, where sin α = 0.05, is 20 m s⁻¹, and its greatest steady speed down the same hill is 30 m s⁻¹. Find P and R.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the greatest steady speed of the car on a level road.

parts.label: a
parts.text: A car of mass 900 kg moves on a level road with its engine working at a constant 30 kW. The resistance to motion is (400 + 2v²) N when the speed is v m s⁻¹. Find the acceleration when v = 25 and state whether the car is speeding up or slowing down.
parts.working: B1 driving force 1200 N. M1 1200 − (400 + 1250) = 900a. A1 a = −0.5, slowing down.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Show that the greatest steady speed V satisfies V³ + 200V − 15 000 = 0 and find V correct to 3 significant figures.
parts.working: M1 30 000/V = 400 + 2V². A1 V³ + 200V − 15 000 = 0. B1 V = 22.0 (by calculator / iteration).

parts.label: a
parts.text: A car of mass 1000 kg accelerates along a straight level road. Its engine works at a constant 25 kW for 20 s, during which its speed increases from 10 m s⁻¹ to 25 m s⁻¹. Find the work done by the engine and the work done against resistance during these 20 s.
parts.answer: 500 000 J by the engine; 237 500 J against resistance
parts.working: B1 WD by engine = 25 000 × 20 = 500 000 J. B1 KE gain = ½ × 1000 × (625 − 100) = 262 500 J. M1 WD against resistance = difference. A1 237 500 J.

parts.label: b
parts.text: The car travels 400 m in this time. Find the average resistance.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Explain why the driving force is not constant during the motion.
parts.answer: Power is constant, so F = P/v decreases as v increases
parts.working: B1 F = P/v and v changes.

practice.subtopic: Work done & power by a force

parts.label: a
parts.text: A box is dragged at constant speed across a horizontal floor by a force of 50 N inclined at 30° above the horizontal. Find the work done by the force when the box moves 8 m.

parts.label: b
parts.text: The box takes 4 s to move the 8 m. Find the average power of the force and the magnitude of the frictional force.
parts.working: B1 346 ÷ 4 = 86.6 W. B1 constant speed so friction = 50 cos 30° = 43.3 N.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Take g = 10 m s⁻². A pump on a farm near Multan raises water from a well. Each minute it lifts 300 kg of water through a vertical height of 15 m and delivers it at a speed of 4 m s⁻¹. Find the work done by the pump each minute.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the power of the pump and the work it does in one hour.

parts.label: a

parts.working: L and E fixed (M1); remaining 4 letters 4! = 24 (A1).

practice.stem: Seven students, including Ali and Sara, stand in a line for a class photograph.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the number of arrangements in which Ali and Sara stand next to each other.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the number of arrangements in which Ali and Sara are not next to each other.

practice.stem: Four-digit numbers are formed from the digits 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7. No digit may be used more than once.

parts.label: a
parts.text: How many different four-digit numbers can be formed?

parts.label: b
parts.text: How many of these are even?

practice.stem: The six letters of the word PLANET are arranged in a line.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the number of arrangements in which the two vowels are next to each other.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the number of arrangements in which the two vowels are not next to each other.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Find the number of arrangements which begin and end with a consonant.

practice.stem: Four boys and three girls, all different, stand in a row.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the number of arrangements in which the three girls stand together.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the number of arrangements in which no two girls stand next to each other.
parts.working: Arrange boys 4! = 24 (B1). 5 gaps, choose and order 3 for the girls: 5 × 4 × 3 = 60 (M1). 24 × 60 = 1440 (A1).

parts.label: c
parts.text: Find the number of arrangements in which boys and girls alternate.

practice.stem: A shelf holds 10 different books: 5 mathematics books, 3 physics books and 2 chemistry books.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the number of ways of arranging the books so that the books of each subject are kept together.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the number of ways of arranging the books so that no two physics books are next to each other.
parts.working: Arrange the other 7 books: 7! = 5040 (B1). 8 gaps, place the 3 physics books: 8 × 7 × 6 = 336 (M1). 5040 × 336 = 1 693 440 (A1).

practice.stem: Five-digit numbers are formed using the digits 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, with no digit repeated.

parts.label: a
parts.text: How many of these numbers are greater than 50 000?

parts.label: b
parts.text: How many of the numbers greater than 50 000 are odd?
parts.working: Case first digit 5 or 7 (odd): last digit from the other 3 odd digits: 2 × 3 × 5 × 4 × 3 = 360 (M1 A1). Case first digit 6: last digit any of 4 odd digits: 1 × 4 × 5 × 4 × 3 = 240 (M1). Total 600 (A1).

practice.stem: Eight people, including Parveen, Qasim and Rehan, stand in a queue.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the number of arrangements in which Parveen and Qasim are at the two ends of the queue.
parts.working: 2 ways for the ends (M1), 6! for the rest: 1440 (A1).

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the number of arrangements in which exactly two of Parveen, Qasim and Rehan are next to each other (the third is not next to either of them).
parts.working: Arrange the other 5 people: 5! = 120 (B1). Choose the pair and its order: 3 × 2 = 6 (M1). Place the pair-unit and the third person in different gaps among the 6 gaps: 6 × 5 = 30 (M1). 120 × 6 × 30 = 21 600 (A1).

practice.stem: Six men and four women, all different, sit in a row of ten seats at a wedding in Faisalabad.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the number of arrangements in which a man sits in each end seat and no two women sit next to each other.
parts.working: Arrange the men: 6! = 720 (B1). Women must go in the 5 gaps between men (not the ends) (M1): 5 × 4 × 3 × 2 = 120 (M1). 720 × 120 = 86 400 (A1).

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the number of arrangements in which all four women sit together.
parts.working: Treat the four women as one unit: 7 units in 7! ways (M1); women within the unit 4! ways: 5040 × 24 = 120 960 (A1).

practice.stem: Numbers between 3000 and 6000 are formed from the digits 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, with no digit repeated.

parts.label: a
parts.text: How many of these numbers are divisible by 5?
parts.working: Last digit must be 5 (B1). First digit 3 or 4 (5 is used) (M1): 2 × 5 × 4 = 40 (A1).

parts.label: b
parts.text: How many of these numbers are odd?
parts.working: First digit 3: last from 1, 5, 7: 3 × 5 × 4 = 60 (M1). First 4: last from 1, 3, 5, 7: 4 × 20 = 80 (A1). First 5: last from 1, 3, 7: 60 (A1). Total 200 (A1).

practice.stem: A committee of 5 people is to be chosen from 7 men and 6 women.

parts.label: a
parts.text: In how many ways can the committee be chosen?

parts.label: b
parts.text: In how many ways can it be chosen if it contains exactly 2 women?

practice.stem: A cricket squad has 15 players, including the captain and the vice-captain. A team of 11 is chosen from the squad.

parts.label: a
parts.text: How many different teams include the captain?

parts.label: b
parts.text: How many different teams include the captain but not the vice-captain?

practice.stem: A team of 4 is to be selected from 5 men and 4 women.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the number of possible teams.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the number of teams that contain at least 2 women.
parts.working: 2 women: ⁴C₂ × ⁵C₂ = 60; 3 women: ⁴C₃ × 5 = 20; 4 women: 1 (M1 A1). Total 81 (A1).

practice.stem: Six students are to be chosen from a class of 12 to represent their school at a science fair in Peshawar. Two of the students, Hina and Bilal, refuse to be in the group together.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the number of possible groups.
parts.working: Total ¹²C₆ = 924 (B1). Groups with both: ¹⁰C₄ = 210 (M1). 924 − 210 = 714 (A1).

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the number of groups that contain Hina but not Bilal.

practice.stem: A restaurant in Lahore offers 6 different starters, 8 different main courses and 4 different desserts.

parts.label: a
parts.text: A customer chooses one starter, one main course and one dessert. How many different meals are possible?

parts.label: b
parts.text: A family chooses 4 different dishes from the whole menu. Find the number of selections that include at least one main course.
parts.working: Total ¹⁸C₄ = 3060 (B1). No main course: ¹⁰C₄ = 210 (M1). 3060 − 210 = 2850 (A1).

practice.stem: A craft box contains 9 different beads: 4 red, 3 blue and 2 green. Five beads are chosen to make a bracelet.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the number of selections that contain at least one bead of each colour.
parts.working: Total ⁹C₅ = 126 (B1). No red: ⁵C₅ = 1; no blue: ⁶C₅ = 6; no green: ⁷C₅ = 21 (M1 A1). Two colours missing is impossible with 5 beads. 126 − 28 = 98 (A1).

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the number of selections with exactly 3 red beads.
parts.working: Choose 3 of the 4 red beads and 2 of the 5 non-red beads: ⁴C₃ × ⁵C₂ (M1) = 4 × 10 = 40 (A1).

practice.stem: Nine volunteers at a flood-relief camp are to be divided into groups.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the number of ways of dividing them into a group of 4, a group of 3 and a group of 2.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the number of ways of dividing them into three groups of 3, where the groups are not labelled.
parts.working: ⁹C₃ × ⁶C₃ × ³C₃ = 1680 (M1). Groups unlabelled: divide by 3! (M1). 1680/6 = 280 (A1).

practice.stem: A project committee of 6 is chosen from 8 Pakistani engineers and 5 Chinese engineers.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the number of committees with more Pakistani than Chinese engineers.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Two of the Pakistani engineers refuse to serve together. Find the number of committees with more Pakistani than Chinese engineers that do not include both of them.
parts.working: Committees containing both: 4P 2C: ⁶C₂ × 10 = 150; 5P 1C: ⁶C₃ × 5 = 100; 6P: ⁶C₄ = 15, total 265 (M1 A1). 1008 − 265 = 743 (A1).

practice.stem: A bag contains 5 red sweets and 4 blue sweets. Three sweets are taken at random without replacement.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the probability that all three sweets are red.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the probability that exactly one sweet is red.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the probability that the committee contains more women than men.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the probability that a particular man, Usman, is on the committee.

practice.stem: A box of 12 LED bulbs contains 3 faulty bulbs. An electrician takes 4 bulbs at random.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the probability that none of the 4 bulbs is faulty.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the probability that at least one is faulty.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Find the probability that exactly 2 are faulty.

practice.stem: Four married couples attend a dinner. Four of the eight people are chosen at random to give short speeches.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the probability that no married couple is chosen.
parts.working: Total ⁸C₄ = 70 (B1). No couple: one person from each couple, 2⁴ = 16 (M1). 16/70 = 8/35 (A1).

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the probability that exactly one married couple is chosen.
parts.working: Choose the couple: 4; choose 2 of the other 3 couples, one person from each: ³C₂ × 2² = 12 (M1). 4 × 12 = 48 (A1). 48/70 = 24/35 (A1).

practice.stem: A debate team of 5 is chosen at random from 7 girls and 6 boys.

parts.label: a

parts.label: b

parts.label: b

parts.label: c

practice.stem: The nine letters of the word ISLAMABAD are arranged in a line.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the number of different arrangements.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the number of different arrangements in which no two A's are next to each other.
parts.working: Arrange I, S, L, M, B, D: 6! = 720 (B1). Choose 3 of the 7 gaps for the A's: ⁷C₃ = 35 (M1). 720 × 35 = 25 200 (A1).

parts.label: c
parts.text: Find the number of different arrangements that begin and end with A.
parts.working: Middle 7 letters I, S, L, M, B, D, A all different: 7! (M1) = 5040 (A1).

practice.stem: The six letters of the word QUETTA are arranged in a random order.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the number of different arrangements.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the probability that the two T's are next to each other.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Find the probability that the arrangement begins and ends with a vowel.
parts.working: Choose and order 2 of the 3 vowels U, E, A for the ends: 3 × 2 = 6 (M1). Middle 4 letters with T twice: 4!/2! = 12 (M1). 72/360 = 1/5 (A1).

parts.label: a

parts.label: a

parts.label: a
parts.text: Describe fully the locus of points in an Argand diagram representing complex numbers z that satisfy |z − 3 + 2i| = 4.
parts.answer: A circle with centre (3, −2), i.e. the point 3 − 2i, and radius 4.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the greatest value of |z| for points on this locus. Give your answer correct to 3 significant figures.
parts.working: M1 distance from origin to centre = √(3² + 2²) = √13; A1 √13 + 4 = 7.61.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The complex number z = x + iy satisfies |z − 1| = |z + 3i|. Describe the locus of z geometrically.
parts.answer: The perpendicular bisector of the line joining the points 1 and −3i (i.e. (1, 0) and (0, −3)).

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the Cartesian equation of the locus in the form ax + by + c = 0.
parts.working: M1 (x − 1)² + y² = x² + (y + 3)²; M1 expand and simplify: −2x + 1 = 6y + 9; A1 x + 3y + 4 = 0.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The locus of z is given by arg(z + 2) = π/3. Find a Cartesian equation for the locus, stating any restriction on x.
parts.working: M1 tan(π/3) = y/(x + 2); A1 with x > −2.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Determine whether the point representing 1 + 3√3 i lies on the locus.
parts.working: M1 z + 2 = 3 + 3√3 i; A1 argument is π/3, so yes.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The complex number z satisfies both |z| = 5 and |z − 6| = 5. Explain why Re z = 3.
parts.answer: z is equidistant from 0 and 6, so it lies on the perpendicular bisector x = 3.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the two possible values of z.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The complex number z satisfies |z − 4 − 3i| = 2. Find the least value of |z|.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the greatest value of arg z for points on this locus. Give your answer in radians correct to 3 significant figures.
parts.working: B1 arg(4 + 3i) = tan⁻¹(3/4) = 0.6435; M1 angle between the line to the centre and the tangent = sin⁻¹(2/5) = 0.4115; A1 0.6435 + 0.4115 = 1.055 ≈ 1.06.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The region R in an Argand diagram consists of points z satisfying both |z − 2 − 3i| ≤ 3 and |z| ≥ |z − 4|. Describe R in words.
parts.answer: The part of the disc with centre 2 + 3i and radius 3 that lies on or to the right of the line Re z = 2 (the perpendicular bisector of 0 and 4).
parts.working: B1 disc centre (2, 3), radius 3; B1 |z| ≥ |z − 4| ⇔ Re z ≥ 2, so R is the right-hand half of the disc.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the greatest value of |z| for points in R. Give your answer correct to 3 significant figures.
parts.working: M1 farthest point lies on the line through O and the centre (it has Re z = 2 + 6/√13 > 2, so it is in R); A1 √13 + 3 = 6.61.

parts.label: c
parts.text: State the least value of Re z for points in R.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The complex number z = x + iy satisfies |z − 4i| = |z − 6|. Find the Cartesian equation of the locus of z.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the least value of |z| for points on this locus, giving your answer correct to 3 significant figures.
parts.working: M1 perpendicular distance from O to 3x − 2y − 5 = 0 is 5/√(9 + 4); A1 1.39.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The locus L₁ is given by arg(z − 1 − i) = ¼π and the locus L₂ by |z − 5 − i| = 3. Describe each locus.
parts.answer: L₁: half-line from the point 1 + i (excluded) at angle π/4 to the positive real direction. L₂: circle centre 5 + i, radius 3.
parts.working: B1 half-line from (1, 1) at 45°; B1 circle.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find, in exact form, the complex numbers represented by the points where L₁ meets L₂.
parts.working: M1 points on L₁: (1 + t) + (1 + t)i, t > 0; M1 (t − 4)² + t² = 9 ⇒ 2t² − 8t + 7 = 0; A1 t = 2 ± √2/2 (both positive, so both points lie on the half-line); A1 both complex numbers.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The complex number z satisfies |z + 2 − i| = 1. Show that the locus of z touches the real axis, and state the point of contact.
parts.answer: Centre −2 + i is 1 unit from the real axis, equal to the radius; contact at z = −2.
parts.working: B1 centre (−2, 1), radius 1; B1 distance to real axis = 1, contact at (−2, 0).

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the least and greatest values of arg z for points on the locus, where −π < arg z ≤ π. Give the least value in radians correct to 3 significant figures.
parts.answer: Least ≈ 2.21 rad (exactly π − 2 tan⁻¹(½)); greatest = π
parts.working: B1 greatest is π, at the point of contact −2; M1 arg(−2 + i) = π − tan⁻¹(½) = 2.678; M1 subtract sin⁻¹(1/√5) = 0.4636 for the other tangent; A1 2.214 ≈ 2.21.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The region R consists of points z satisfying |z − 3i| ≤ 2 and Re z ≥ 1. Find the least value of arg z for points in R. Give your answer in radians correct to 3 significant figures, and show that the point where it occurs is in R.
parts.answer: ≈ 0.841 rad (π/2 − sin⁻¹(2/3)); at the tangent point Re z = 2√5/3 ≈ 1.49 ≥ 1
parts.working: M1 tangent from O to circle centre 3i, radius 2; M1 angle = π/2 − sin⁻¹(2/3); A1 0.841; B1 tangent length √(9 − 4) = √5, so Re z = √5 cos(π/2 − sin⁻¹(2/3)) = √5 × 2/3 = 2√5/3 ≈ 1.49 ≥ 1.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the greatest value of |z| for points in R. Give your answer correct to 3 significant figures.
parts.working: M1 on the circle x² + (y − 3)² = 4 we have |z|² = 6y − 5, so maximise y subject to x ≥ 1; M1 x = 1 gives y = 3 + √3; A1 |z| = √(13 + 6√3) = 4.84.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The complex numbers z and w are given by z = 3 − 4i and w = 1 + 2i. Find zw in the form x + iy.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find z/w in the form x + iy, showing all necessary working.
parts.working: M1 multiply numerator and denominator by 1 − 2i; M1 denominator 5; A1 (−5 − 10i)/5 = −1 − 2i.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Solve the equation z² − 6z + 13 = 0, giving your answers in the form x + iy.
parts.working: M1 use the formula or complete the square; M1 √(36 − 52) = √(−16) = 4i; A1 3 ± 2i.

parts.label: b
parts.text: State the sum and the product of the two roots.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Express (3 + 2i)/(4 − i) in the form x + iy, where x and y are exact fractions.
parts.working: M1 multiply by (4 + i)/(4 + i); M1 denominator 17, numerator 12 + 3i + 8i − 2 = 10 + 11i; A1.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the modulus of (3 + 2i)/(4 − i), giving your answer in exact form.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the complex number z satisfying 2z + 3iz* = 7 + 8i, where z* is the complex conjugate of z. Give your answer in the form x + iy.
parts.working: M1 substitute z = x + iy, z* = x − iy; M1 2x + 2iy + 3ix + 3y; M1 equate real and imaginary parts: 2x + 3y = 7, 3x + 2y = 8; A1 x = 2; A1 y = 1.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The complex number u is given by u = (7 + i)/(1 − i). Express u in the form x + iy, showing all your working.
parts.working: M1 multiply by (1 + i)/(1 + i); A1 (6 + 8i)/2 = 3 + 4i.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find u² in the form x + iy.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Given that u² + pu + q = 0, where p and q are real, find p and q.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The complex number w = a + 3i, where a is real, satisfies |w − 2| = 5. Find the two possible values of a.

parts.label: b
parts.text: For the value of a with a > 2, find w² and arg(w²), giving the argument in radians correct to 3 significant figures.

parts.label: a
parts.text:
Solve the simultaneous equations
(1 + i)z + w = 1 + 2i
2z + iw = 3 + 6i,
giving z and w in the form x + iy.
parts.working: M1 eliminate w: multiply first by i: (i − 1)z + iw = i − 2; M1 subtract from second: (3 − i)z = 5 + 5i; M1 z = (5 + 5i)/(3 − i) = (5 + 5i)(3 + i)/10; A1 z = 1 + 2i; M1 w = 1 + 2i − (1 + i)(1 + 2i); A1 w = 2 − i.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the complex numbers z which satisfy the equation zz* + 2iz = 12 + 6i, where z* is the complex conjugate of z.
parts.working: M1 put z = x + iy: x² + y² + 2ix − 2y = 12 + 6i; M1 equate parts: 2x = 6, x² + y² − 2y = 12; A1 x = 3; M1 y² − 2y − 3 = 0; A1 y = 3 or −1.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The complex number z is given by z = −1 + √3 i. Find the modulus and argument of z, giving the argument as an exact multiple of π.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Write z in the form re^{iθ} and hence find z³.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The complex numbers z and w are given by z = 2e^{iπ/6} and w = 3e^{−iπ/4}. Find zw and z/w, each in the form re^{iθ} with r > 0 and −π < θ ≤ π.
parts.working: M1 multiply moduli, add arguments; A1 zw; A1 z/w (divide moduli, subtract arguments).

parts.label: b
parts.text: Express zw in the form x + iy, giving x and y correct to 3 significant figures.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The complex number z is given by z = 4e^{iπ/3}. Find z³, giving your answer in the form x + iy.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the smallest positive integer n for which zⁿ is real and positive, and state the value of zⁿ in this case.
