parts.text: A student found the variance of a random sample of 25 values by dividing Σ(x − x̄)² by 25, obtaining 18.4. Find an unbiased estimate of the population variance.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Explain why dividing by n tends to underestimate the population variance.
parts.answer: Deviations are measured from the sample mean, which is the value that minimises Σ(x − a)²; so Σ(x − x̄)² is on average smaller than Σ(x − μ)², and dividing by n − 1 corrects this
parts.working: B1 deviations from x̄ rather than μ. B1 Σ(x − x̄)² ≤ Σ(x − μ)², so dividing by n gives values that are too small on average.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The amount a customer spends in a café has mean Rs 400 and standard deviation Rs 120; the distribution is not normal. A random sample of 50 customers is taken. State the approximate distribution of the sample mean amount spent, giving its parameters.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the probability that the sample mean is more than Rs 420.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The number of phone calls received per day by a helpline follows a Poisson distribution with mean 3.6. The numbers of calls on 40 randomly chosen days are recorded. Use a suitable approximation to find the probability that the mean number of calls per day for these 40 days is less than 3.3.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Explain why the Central Limit Theorem is needed in part (a).
parts.answer: The population (number of calls) is not normally distributed

parts.label: a
parts.text: A fair six-sided die is thrown. Show that the score X has mean 3.5 and variance 35/12.

parts.label: b
parts.text: The die is thrown 60 times. Find the approximate probability that the mean score is greater than 3.8.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The masses of parcels handled by a courier have standard deviation 5 kg and unknown mean μ. A random sample of n parcels is taken, where n is large. Find the smallest n such that the probability that the sample mean exceeds μ by more than 1 kg is less than 0.05.

parts.label: b
parts.text: State why the answer to part (a) does not depend on the distribution of the masses being normal.
parts.answer: n is large, so the sample mean is approximately normal by the Central Limit Theorem

parts.label: a
parts.text: The time taken to process a visa application has mean 5 minutes and standard deviation 1.5 minutes. An officer processes 100 randomly chosen applications in one shift. Find the approximate probability that the total processing time is more than 520 minutes.
parts.working: M1 total T: mean 500, variance 100 × 1.5² = 225. M1 approximately normal by CLT. M1 z = 20/15 = 1.333. A1 0.0912.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the time t such that the officer has a 95% chance of finishing 100 applications within t minutes.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The continuous random variable X has probability density function f(x) = 3x²/8 for 0 ≤ x ≤ 2, and f(x) = 0 otherwise. Show that E(X) = 1.5 and Var(X) = 0.15.

parts.label: b
parts.text: A random sample of 40 observations of X is taken. Find the approximate probability that the sample mean is less than 1.45.

parts.label: a
parts.text: A college in Rawalpindi has 600 students. The principal wants a random sample of 30 students to answer a questionnaire about the canteen. Describe how random numbers could be used to choose the sample.
parts.answer: Number the students 001 to 600; use random numbers (calculator, computer or table) to generate three-digit numbers; select the students with those numbers, ignoring numbers above 600 and repeats, until 30 are chosen
parts.working: B1 list and number all 600 students. B1 generate random numbers in the range 001–600. B1 ignore repeats/out-of-range values and continue until 30 chosen.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Explain why the principal might use a sample rather than ask all 600 students.
parts.answer: Quicker and cheaper / less effort than a census

parts.label: a
parts.text: A transport researcher wants to estimate the proportion of adults in a city who use public transport. She interviews people waiting at a Metro bus station between 8 am and 9 am on a Monday. Explain why this sample is likely to be biased.
parts.answer: People at a bus station are already public-transport users, and the time chosen only includes people commuting at that hour, so public-transport use will be overestimated
parts.working: B1 only people at a bus station (users) are sampled. B1 particular time/day excludes other groups; estimate too high.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Suggest a better method of obtaining a sample.
parts.answer: Choose a random sample from a list of all adults in the city (e.g. electoral roll) using random numbers, and contact them
parts.working: B1 use a sampling frame of all adults. B1 random selection.

parts.label: a
parts.text:
The 75 members of a cricket club are numbered 01 to 75. The secretary uses the following two-digit random numbers, read from left to right, to choose a sample of 5 members:
53 82 07 53 66 91 24 75 00 38
Write down the numbers of the members chosen, explaining how any unsuitable numbers are dealt with.
parts.working: B1 ignore 82, 91 and 00 (out of range). B1 ignore the second 53 (repeat). B1 53, 07, 66, 24, 75.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Explain the difference between a population and a sample, and state one reason why a sample should be random.
parts.answer: The population is all members of the club; a sample is a subset of them. Random sampling gives every member an equal chance of selection, avoiding bias
parts.working: B1 population/sample distinction. B1 avoids bias / allows valid inference.

practice.stem: Take g = 10 m s⁻². Particles A and B, of masses 3 kg and m kg (m > 3), are connected by a light inextensible string over a fixed smooth pulley and released from rest. parts.working: Friction acts down the plane: a = g sin 25° + 0.3g cos 25° (M1 A1) = 6.95 m s⁻² (A1).

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the distance it travels up the plane before coming to instantaneous rest.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Show that the particle then slides back down, and find its speed when it returns to its starting point.
parts.answer: tan 25° = 0.466 > 0.3, so it slides; speed 3.73 m s⁻¹
parts.working: tan 25° > μ, so the weight component exceeds limiting friction (B1). Down: a = 10(sin 25° − 0.3 cos 25°) = 1.5073 (M1 A1). v = √(2 × 1.5073 × 4.6076) = 3.73 m s⁻¹ (A1).

practice.stem: Take g = 10 m s⁻². A block of mass 4 kg rests on a rough plane inclined at 30° to the horizontal, with coefficient of friction 0.2. practice.stem: Take g = 10 m s⁻². A box of mass 6 kg is on a rough ramp inclined at 10° to the horizontal at a warehouse in Faisalabad. A rope pulls the box with a force of 30 N acting at 15° above the line of greatest slope, up the ramp. The box is about to move up the ramp.

practice.stem: Take g = 10 m s⁻². A particle of mass 2.5 kg is on a rough plane inclined at 35° to the horizontal. The coefficient of friction is 0.4. A force of magnitude P N acts on the particle at an angle of 20° above the line of greatest slope, directed up the plane.

practice.stem: Take g = 10 m s⁻².

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the greatest angle of a slope on which a block can rest without any applied force, if the coefficient of friction is 0.5.

parts.text: A block of mass 3 kg is placed on a slope inclined at 40° with the same coefficient of friction, and a force of 12 N acts on it up the line of greatest slope. Determine whether the block remains at rest, and find the magnitude and direction of the frictional force.
parts.answer: Remains at rest; friction 7.28 N up the slope
parts.working: M1 R = 30 cos 40° = 22.98 N; A1 maximum friction 11.49 N; M1 force needed to hold: 30 sin 40° − 12 = 7.28 N; A1 7.28 < 11.49 so at rest; A1 friction 7.28 N acting up the slope.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Three horizontal forces act on a particle: 12 N due east, 9 N due north and 5 N due west. Find the magnitude of the resultant force and the angle it makes with due east.

practice.stem: Three horizontal ropes pull on a ring fixed to a post on a boat at Keamari harbour. The forces are 25 N on a bearing of 040°, 18 N on a bearing of 160° and 30 N on a bearing of 270°.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the magnitude of the resultant force and its bearing.
parts.working: M1 resolve east: 25 sin 40° + 18 sin 160° − 30 = −7.774; M1 resolve north: 25 cos 40° + 18 cos 160° = 2.237; A1 both components; M1 magnitude √(7.774² + 2.237²); A1 8.09 N; A1 bearing 270° + tan⁻¹(2.237/7.774) = 286°.

practice.stem: Three forces act at a point O: 6 N along the positive x-axis, 8 N along the positive y-axis, and F N acting in the third quadrant at an angle θ below the negative x-axis. The resultant of the three forces is 5 N along the positive y-axis.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find F and θ.
parts.working: M1 resolve along x: 6 − F cos θ = 0; M1 resolve along y: 8 − F sin θ = 5; A1 F cos θ = 6, F sin θ = 3; A1 F = √45 = 6.71; A1 θ = tan⁻¹(0.5) = 26.6°.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Two forces of magnitudes P N and Q N act at a point, and the angle between their directions is 130°. Their resultant has magnitude 20 N and is perpendicular to the force of magnitude P N. Find Q and P.
parts.working: M1 resolve along P: P + Q cos 130° = 0; M1 resolve perpendicular to P: Q sin 130° = 20; A1 Q = 20/sin 50° = 26.1; M1 P = Q cos 50°; A1 16.8.

practice.stem: Take g = 10 m s⁻². A lantern of mass 2 kg hangs in equilibrium from two light strings. One string makes an angle of 30° with the horizontal and the other makes an angle of 60° with the horizontal, on the other side.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the tension in each string.
parts.working: M1 resolve horizontally: T₁ cos 30° = T₂ cos 60°; M1 resolve vertically: T₁ sin 30° + T₂ sin 60° = 20; A1 one equation solved for a ratio, T₂ = √3 T₁; A1 T₁ = 10 N; A1 T₂ = 17.3 N.

practice.stem: Take g = 10 m s⁻². A particle of mass 0.8 kg hangs in equilibrium from two light strings, each making an angle of 40° with the vertical.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the tension in each string.
parts.working: M1 by symmetry the tensions are equal; M1 2T cos 40° = 8; A1 T = 5.22 N.

practice.stem: Take g = 10 m s⁻². A ball of mass 3 kg is attached to one end of a light string whose other end is fixed. The ball is held in equilibrium, with the string taut, by a horizontal force of 12 N.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the angle the string makes with the vertical and the tension in the string.
parts.working: M1 resolve: T sin α = 12, T cos α = 30; A1 tan α = 0.4, α = 21.8°; M1 T = √(12² + 30²); A1 32.3 N.

practice.stem: Take g = 10 m s⁻². Two points A and B are on a horizontal ceiling, 1.0 m apart. A particle C of mass 5 kg is attached to light inextensible strings AC and BC, of lengths 0.8 m and 0.6 m, and hangs in equilibrium below AB.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Show that angle ACB is a right angle, and find the angles that AC and BC make with the horizontal.
parts.answer: AC at 36.9°, BC at 53.1° to the horizontal

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the tensions in AC and BC.
parts.working: M1 horizontal: 0.8 T_A = 0.6 T_B; M1 vertical: 0.6 T_A + 0.8 T_B = 50; A1 T_A = 30 N; A1 T_B = 40 N.

practice.stem: A particle of weight 20 N hangs in equilibrium from two light strings. One string has tension 15 N and makes an angle of 25° above the horizontal. The other string, on the opposite side, has tension T N and makes an angle θ above the horizontal.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find T and θ.
parts.working: M1 horizontal: T cos θ = 15 cos 25°; M1 vertical: T sin θ + 15 sin 25° = 20; A1 T cos θ = 13.59, T sin θ = 13.66; A1 T = 19.3; A1 θ = 45.1°.

practice.stem: A light inextensible string of length 1.8 m has its ends fixed at points A and B on the same horizontal level, 1.2 m apart. A small smooth ring of weight 6 N is threaded on the string.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The ring hangs at rest at the midpoint of the string. Find the tension in the string, correct to 3 significant figures.
parts.working: M1 each half 0.9 m with horizontal 0.6 m, so vertical drop √(0.9² − 0.6²) = √0.45 = 0.671 m and sine of angle to horizontal = 0.671/0.9 = 0.745; M1 2T × 0.745 = 6; A1 T = 4.02 N.

parts.label: b
parts.text: A horizontal force of magnitude F N, acting in the direction from A to B, is now applied to the ring, so that it rests vertically below B with both parts of the string taut. Show that the ring is 0.5 m below B, and find the tension in the string and the value of F.
parts.working: M1 AR = 1.8 − BR and AR² = 1.2² + BR², so (1.8 − d)² = 1.44 + d²; A1 d = 0.5, AR = 1.3; B1 tension the same in both parts (smooth ring); M1 vertical: T + T × (5/13) = 6, so T = 13/3 = 4.33 N; A1 horizontal: F = T × 12/13 = 4 N.

practice.subtopic: Equilibrium of a particle (forces at a point)

parts.label: a
parts.text: A particle is in equilibrium under three horizontal forces: 6 N due east, 8 N due north and a third force. Find the magnitude and bearing of the third force.
parts.working: M1 third force has components 6 W and 8 S; A1 10 N; A1 bearing 180° + tan⁻¹(6/8) = 216.9°.

practice.subtopic: Equilibrium of a particle (forces at a point)
practice.stem: A particle of weight 12 N rests on a smooth plane inclined at 30° to the horizontal. It is held in equilibrium by a horizontal force of magnitude P N acting towards the plane.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the value of P and the normal reaction.
parts.working: M1 resolve vertically: R cos 30° = 12; A1 R = 13.9 N; M1 resolve horizontally: P = R sin 30°; A1 P = 12 tan 30° = 6.93.

practice.subtopic: Equilibrium of a particle (forces at a point)
practice.stem: Three forces of magnitudes 10 N, P N and Q N act on a particle, which is in equilibrium. The 10 N force acts at 30° above the positive x-axis, the P N force acts along the negative x-axis and the Q N force acts at 60° below the positive x-axis.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the values of P and Q.
parts.working: M1 resolve vertically: 10 sin 30° = Q sin 60°; A1 Q = 5.77; M1 resolve horizontally: P = 10 cos 30° + Q cos 60°; A1 cos values correct; A1 P = 11.5.

practice.subtopic: Equilibrium of a particle (forces at a point)
practice.stem: A particle is in equilibrium under three forces. Two of them have magnitudes 12 N and 15 N, and the angle between their directions is 70°.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the magnitude of the third force.
parts.working: M1 third force balances the resultant of the other two; M1 R² = 12² + 15² + 2(12)(15) cos 70°; A1 22.2 N.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the angle between the third force and the 12 N force.
parts.working: M1 angle between resultant and 12 N force: sin φ = 15 sin 70°/22.18; A1 φ = 39.4°; A1 third force at 180° − 39.4° = 140.6° to the 12 N force.

practice.subtopic: Equilibrium of a particle (forces at a point)
practice.stem: A particle is in equilibrium under four forces: 8 N along the positive x-axis, 6 N along the positive y-axis, 10 N acting at an angle θ above the negative x-axis, and F N along the negative y-axis.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find θ and F.
parts.working: M1 resolve along x: 10 cos θ = 8; A1 θ = 36.9°; M1 resolve along y: 6 + 10 sin θ = F; A1 F = 12.

practice.subtopic: Equilibrium of a particle (forces at a point)

parts.label: a
parts.text: Three forces of magnitudes 20 N, 25 N and 30 N act at a point and are in equilibrium. Find the angle between the directions of the 20 N and 25 N forces.
parts.working: M1 resultant of 20 N and 25 N has magnitude 30 N; M1 30² = 20² + 25² + 2(20)(25) cos θ; A1 cos θ = −0.125, θ = 97.2°.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the other two angles between the directions of the forces.

practice.stem: Take g = 10 m s⁻². A box of mass 6 kg rests on rough horizontal ground. The coefficient of friction is 0.35. A horizontal force of 15 N acts on the box.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Determine whether the box moves, and state the magnitude of the frictional force.
parts.answer: It does not move; friction is 15 N
parts.working: M1 R = 60 N; A1 maximum friction 0.35 × 60 = 21 N; A1 15 < 21, so at rest with friction 15 N.

practice.stem: Take g = 10 m s⁻². A crate of mass 10 kg on rough horizontal ground is pulled by a rope inclined at 25° above the horizontal. The tension in the rope is 40 N and the crate is about to move.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the coefficient of friction.
parts.working: M1 resolve vertically: R + 40 sin 25° = 100; A1 R = 83.1 N; M1 resolve horizontally: F = 40 cos 25° = 36.25 N; M1 μ = F/R; A1 0.436.

practice.stem: Take g = 10 m s⁻². A worker pushes a box of mass 12 kg across a rough horizontal floor with a force of magnitude P N directed at 30° below the horizontal. The coefficient of friction is 0.25.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the value of P for which the box is about to move.
parts.working: M1 resolve vertically: R = 120 + P sin 30°; M1 resolve horizontally: P cos 30° = F; M1 F = 0.25R; A1 P(cos 30° − 0.25 sin 30°) = 30; A1 P = 40.5.

practice.stem: Take g = 10 m s⁻². A sack of rice of mass 20 kg lies on a rough horizontal floor in a godown. The coefficient of friction is 0.5. A force of magnitude P N is applied at an angle θ above the horizontal.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Show that the sack is about to move when P = 100/(cos θ + 0.5 sin θ).
parts.working: M1 R = 200 − P sin θ; M1 P cos θ = 0.5R; A1 rearrange to the given result.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the value of P when θ = 30°, and the corresponding normal reaction.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Compare your answer to part (b) with the force needed when the sack is pulled horizontally, and explain the difference.
parts.answer: Horizontal pull needs P = 100 N, more than 89.6 N; pulling upwards reduces the normal reaction and hence the maximum friction
parts.working: B1 θ = 0 gives P = 100 N > 89.6 N; B1 the upward component reduces R, so limiting friction 0.5R is smaller.

practice.stem:
The times, in minutes, taken by 15 students in Karachi to travel to college one morning are shown in the stem-and-leaf diagram.
1 | 2 5 8
2 | 1 2 4 5 7 8
3 | 1 3 6 8
4 | 2
5 | 5
Key: 2 | 4 means 24 minutes

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the median and the interquartile range of the times.
parts.answer: Median 27 minutes; LQ 21, UQ 36, IQR 15 minutes
parts.working:
B1 median 27
B1 quartiles 21 and 36
B1 IQR 15

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the mean time, correct to 3 significant figures.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Give a reason why the median may be a better average than the mean for these data.
parts.answer: The value 55 is much larger than the rest (data positively skewed), so it pulls the mean up; the median is not affected by extreme values

practice.stem:
The marks out of 50 scored in a quiz by 11 students in class P and 11 students in class Q are shown in the back-to-back stem-and-leaf diagram. Leaves for class P are on the left.
8 | 1 |
9 5 2 | 2 | 1 6
7 4 3 1 | 3 | 0 2 5 8 8
7 4 0 | 4 | 1 3 5 9
Key: 5 | 2 | 6 means 25 marks for a student in class P and 26 marks for a student in class Q

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the median and the interquartile range for each class.
parts.answer: Class P: median 33, IQR 40 − 25 = 15. Class Q: median 38, IQR 43 − 30 = 13
parts.working:
B1 medians 33 and 38
B1 quartiles for P: 25, 40
B1 quartiles for Q: 30, 43
B1 IQRs 15 and 13

parts.label: b
parts.text: Make two comparisons between the marks of the two classes.
parts.answer: Class Q scored higher on average (median 38 > 33); Class Q's marks were slightly less spread (IQR 13 < 15)
parts.working:
B1 average comparison in context
B1 spread comparison in context

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the range and the median of the battery lives.

practice.stem:
A botanist in Murree measured the heights, in cm, of 19 young pine seedlings after one year. The results are shown below.
3 | 4
4 | 1 5 7 8
5 | 2 3 5 6 8 9
6 | 1 2 4 6 7
7 | 1 4
8 | 
9 | 6
Key: 5 | 3 means 53 cm

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the median and the quartiles of the heights.
parts.answer: Median 58 cm, LQ 48 cm, UQ 66 cm

parts.label: b
parts.text: An outlier is defined as any value more than 1.5 × IQR above the upper quartile or below the lower quartile. Determine whether there are any outliers, showing your working.
parts.answer: IQR = 18; 1.5 × 18 = 27; limits 21 and 93; 96 > 93 so 96 cm is an outlier; no low outliers
parts.working:
M1 1.5 × 18 = 27
A1 limits 21 and 93
A1 96 is the only outlier

parts.label: c
parts.text: Suggest one reason why the researcher might keep the value 96 in the data.
parts.answer: It may be a genuine measurement of an unusually tall plant, not a mistake

parts.label: a
parts.text:
The stem-and-leaf diagram shows the masses, in grams, of 15 guavas from a market stall, where x is an unknown digit.
3 | 2 5 8
4 | 0 1 3 x 6 7 9
5 | 0 2 4 7 8
Key: 4 | 1 means 41 g
Given that the mean mass is 45.8 g, find the value of x.
parts.working:
M1 sum of the other 14 values = 642
M1 642 + 40 + x = 15 × 45.8 = 687
A1 x = 5

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the interquartile range of the masses.

The rainfall, in mm, recorded on 19 days in August at a weather station in Abbottabad was:

parts.label: a
parts.text: Represent the data in a stem-and-leaf diagram with stems 0, 1, 2, 3, 4 and a key.
parts.working:
B1 correct stems
B1 leaves correct and ordered
B1 key

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the median and the interquartile range.
parts.working:
B1 median 19
B1 quartiles 13 and 26
B1 IQR 13

practice.stem:
The resting pulse rates, in beats per minute, of 15 athletes and 15 non-athletes at a sports club in Faisalabad are shown. Leaves for athletes are on the left.
8 | 4 |
8 8 6 5 3 2 | 5 |
9 6 4 3 1 0 | 6 | 2 5 8
4 1 | 7 | 0 1 2 4 5 6 8 9
| 8 | 1 4 8
| 9 | 3
Key: 8 | 5 | 2 means 58 for an athlete and 52 for a non-athlete

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the median and the quartiles for each group.
parts.answer: Athletes: LQ 55, median 60, UQ 66. Non-athletes: LQ 70, median 75, UQ 81
parts.working:
B1 both medians
B1 B1 quartiles for each group
B1 all correct

parts.label: b
parts.text: Compare the resting pulse rates of the two groups in two different ways.
parts.answer: Athletes have lower pulse rates on average (median 60 vs 75); the spreads are similar (both IQRs 11), although the non-athletes have a larger range (31 vs 26)
parts.working:
B1 average
B1 spread (both IQRs are 11; ranges 26 and 31)

parts.label: c
parts.text: State one advantage of a back-to-back stem-and-leaf diagram over two box-and-whisker plots for these data.
parts.answer: It shows every individual value (the raw data are kept), so the shape of each distribution can be seen in detail

parts.label: a
parts.text:
The ages, in years, of 11 members of a cricket club committee are, in order,
22  25  28  31  33  3a  41  4b  50  54  59
where a and b are unknown digits. The median age is 37 years and the mean age is 39 years. Find a and b.
parts.working:

M1 total 11 × 39 = 429
A1 4b = 429 − 380 = 49, so b = 9

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the interquartile range of the ages.

practice.stem:

A1 total 150

practice.stem:
The ages, a years, of 80 visitors to a museum in Lahore one morning are shown in a histogram. The frequency densities (heights) of some bars and the frequencies of some classes are known:

10 ≤ a < 20: bar height 1.6
20 ≤ a < 40: frequency 24, bar height 1.2
40 ≤ a < 70: frequency 18
70 ≤ a < 90: frequency unknown

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the frequency of the class 10 ≤ a < 20 and the frequency density of the class 70 ≤ a < 90.
parts.working:
B1 scale: 24 ÷ 20 = 1.2 matches, so height = frequency density
B1 1.6 × 10 = 16
M1 80 − 8 − 16 − 24 − 18 = 14
A1 14 ÷ 20 = 0.7

parts.label: b
parts.text: State which class contains the median age.
parts.working: B1 the 40th/41st values lie in 20–40 (cumulative 24 then 48)

practice.stem:
The typing speeds, w words per minute, of 120 applicants for an office job in Rawalpindi are summarised in a cumulative frequency table. The slowest applicant typed more than 10 words per minute. Assume the points of the cumulative frequency graph are joined by straight lines.
w ≤ 20: 6
w ≤ 30: 20
w ≤ 40: 52

w ≤ 70: 120

practice.stem:
A call centre in Karachi recorded the durations, t minutes, of 100 calls.
Duration t: 0 ≤ t < 2 | 2 ≤ t < 5 | 5 ≤ t < 10 | 10 ≤ t < 20 | 20 ≤ t < 30

practice.stem: The daily maximum temperatures, in °C, in Jacobabad over 31 days in June have the following summary: lowest 39, lower quartile 43, median 44, upper quartile 47, highest 54.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the interquartile range and determine whether the highest temperature is an outlier, where an outlier is a value more than 1.5 × IQR above the upper quartile.
parts.answer: IQR = 4; 47 + 6 = 53; 54 > 53, so it is an outlier

parts.label: b

practice.stem:
The numbers of customers served in each of 15 half-hour periods at a bank counter in Gujranwala were:
0 | 5 8
1 | 2 4 5 7 8
2 | 0 1 3 4 6 9
3 | 3
4 | 7
Key: 2 | 3 means 23 customers

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the five values needed to draw a box-and-whisker plot of the data.
parts.working:
B1 median
B1 quartiles
B1 extremes

parts.label: b
parts.text: Show that 47 is an outlier using the 1.5 × IQR rule, and state the value at which the upper whisker would end if outliers are plotted separately.
parts.answer: IQR 12, 26 + 18 = 44, 47 > 44 so outlier; whisker ends at 33

practice.stem:
Box-and-whisker plots summarise the waiting times, in minutes, at two clinics in Rawalpindi on one day.
Clinic A: lowest 4, lower quartile 9, median 13, upper quartile 20, highest 35
Clinic B: lowest 6, lower quartile 10, median 12, upper quartile 14, highest 18

parts.label: a
parts.text: Compare the waiting times at the two clinics in two ways.
parts.answer: Clinic A has a slightly higher median (13 vs 12); Clinic A is much more spread out (IQR 11 vs 4, range 31 vs 12)

parts.label: b
parts.text: Clinic A saw 120 patients that day. Estimate how many of them waited between 9 and 20 minutes.
parts.working: B1 half of the patients lie between the quartiles

parts.label: c
parts.text: A manager says: 'At clinic B no patient waited more than 18 minutes, but at clinic A at least a quarter of patients waited longer than any patient at clinic B.' Use the box plots to decide whether this statement is justified.
parts.answer: Justified: clinic B's maximum is 18, and clinic A's upper quartile is 20 > 18, so at least 25% of clinic A patients waited at least 20 minutes, longer than any clinic B patient
parts.working:
M1 compare UQ of A with max of B
A1 conclusion

practice.stem:
Two varieties of wheat were grown on 40 one-hectare plots each in Punjab. The yields, in tonnes per hectare, are summarised:
Variety X: mean 3.42, standard deviation 0.31
Variety Y: mean 3.58, standard deviation 0.62

parts.label: a
parts.text: Compare the yields of the two varieties in two ways.
parts.answer: Variety Y has the higher mean yield (3.58 > 3.42 t/ha); variety X's yields are more consistent (sd 0.31 < 0.62)
parts.working:
B1 average in context
B1 spread in context

parts.label: b
parts.text: A farmer wants a reliable harvest every year. Suggest which variety the farmer should choose, giving a reason.
parts.answer: Variety X: its standard deviation is half that of Y, so yields vary less, even though its mean is slightly lower

parts.label: c
parts.text: Estimate the total yield from 25 hectares of variety Y. Also state the mean and the standard deviation of the yields of variety Y in kilograms per hectare.
parts.answer: 89.5 tonnes; mean 3580 kg/ha, standard deviation 620 kg/ha
parts.working:
B1 25 × 3.58 = 89.5 tonnes
B1 3580 and 620 (both multiplied by 1000)

practice.stem:
The monthly incomes, in thousands of rupees, of 9 workers at factory P in Sialkot are:
32  35  35  38  40  41  44  46  180

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the mean and the median of the monthly incomes of the workers at factory P.
parts.answer: Mean 54.6 thousand rupees (491/9); median 40 thousand rupees

parts.label: b
parts.text: Explain which average better represents a typical worker at factory P.
parts.answer: The median: the mean is pulled up by the single very high income of 180

parts.label: c
parts.text: At factory Q, the monthly incomes of 9 workers have median 42 thousand rupees and mean 43 thousand rupees. A worker claims that the workers at factory P earn more because 54.6 > 43. Comment on this claim.
parts.answer: Not justified: the high mean at P is due to one outlier (180); the median at Q (42) is higher than at P (40), so a typical worker at Q earns slightly more
parts.working:
M1 compare medians
A1 conclusion with reason

parts.label: a
parts.text: The point P(5, 3) lies on the circle (x − 2)² + (y + 1)² = 25. Find the gradient of the radius through P.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the equation of the tangent to the circle at P, giving your answer in the form ax + by = c.
parts.working: M1 tangent gradient = −3/4 (negative reciprocal). M1 y − 3 = −¾(x − 5). A1 3x + 4y = 27.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The circle C has equation x² + y² − 6x − 4y − 12 = 0. Find the centre and radius of C, and show that the point A(7, 5) lies on C.
parts.working: M1 (x − 3)² + (y − 2)² = 25. A1 centre (3, 2), r = 5. B1 substitution of (7, 5) gives 25.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the equation of the normal to C at A.
parts.working: M1 the normal passes through the centre: gradient (5 − 2)/(7 − 3) = 3/4. A1 3x − 4y = 1.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Find the equation of the tangent to C at A.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The normals to a circle at the points A(1, 4) and B(3, −2) have equations y = 2x + 2 and x + 2y = −1 respectively. Find the coordinates of the centre of the circle.
parts.working: M1 solve simultaneously: x + 2(2x + 2) = −1. A1 x = −1, y = 0.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the equation of the circle.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Find the equation of the tangent to the circle at B.
parts.working: M1 tangent ⟂ normal (gradient −½), so tangent gradient 2. A1 y + 2 = 2(x − 3), y = 2x − 8.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The points A(5, 5) and B(7, −1) lie on the circle x² + y² = 50. Find the equations of the tangents to the circle at A and at B.
parts.answer: At A: x + y = 10; at B: 7x − y = 50
parts.working: M1 gradient OA = 1 so tangent gradient −1. A1 x + y = 10. M1 gradient OB = −1/7 so tangent gradient 7. A1 7x − y = 50.

parts.label: b
parts.text: The tangents meet at T. Find the coordinates of T and show that TA = TB.
parts.working: M1 solve simultaneously. A1 T(7.5, 2.5). A1 TA² = 2.5² + 2.5² = 12.5 and TB² = 0.5² + 3.5² = 12.5.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The point P(6, 7) lies on the circle (x − 4)² + (y − 3)² = 20. Find the equation of the tangent to the circle at P.
parts.working: M1 radius gradient (7 − 3)/(6 − 4) = 2. M1 tangent gradient −½. A1 y − 7 = −½(x − 6), x + 2y = 20.

parts.label: b
parts.text: The tangent meets the x-axis at Q and the y-axis at R. Find the area of triangle OQR, where O is the origin.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Find the exact length PQ.

parts.label: a
parts.text: A circle has equation (x + 1)² + (y − 2)² = 10. Show that the point T(5, 4) lies outside the circle.
parts.answer: Distance from centre (−1, 2) to T is √40 > √10

parts.label: b
parts.text: A tangent is drawn from T to touch the circle at S. Find the exact length TS.
parts.working: M1 angle CST = 90°, so TS² = CT² − r² = 40 − 10. A1 TS = √30.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Find the area of the kite formed by T, the centre C and the two points of contact of the tangents from T.
parts.working: M1 two right-angled triangles each of area ½ × √10 × √30. A1 √300 = 10√3.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Lines of gradient 2 are tangents to the circle x² + y² = 20. By considering the equation y = 2x + c, find the two possible values of c.
parts.working: M1 substitute: x² + (2x + c)² = 20 → 5x² + 4cx + c² − 20 = 0. M1 discriminant = 0: 16c² − 20(c² − 20) = 0. A1 c² = 100. A1 c = ±10.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the coordinates of the points of contact.
parts.working: M1 x = −4c/10 (repeated root). A1 (−4, 2) for c = 10 and (4, −2) for c = −10.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The line y = mx passes through the origin and is a tangent to the circle (x − 6)² + (y − 2)² = 4. Show that 32m² − 24m = 0.
parts.answer: Substituting gives (1 + m²)x² − (12 + 4m)x + 36 = 0; discriminant (12 + 4m)² − 144(1 + m²) = 0 simplifies to 32m² − 24m = 0 (after dividing by −4)
parts.working: M1 substitute y = mx and expand: (1 + m²)x² − (12 + 4m)x + 36 = 0. M1 use b² − 4ac = 0. A1 (12 + 4m)² = 144(1 + m²). A1 −128m² + 96m = 0, i.e. 32m² − 24m = 0.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Hence find the equations of the two tangents from the origin to the circle and the coordinates of the point of contact on the tangent that is not an axis.
parts.answer: y = 0 and y = ¾x; point of contact (4.8, 3.6)

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the coordinates of the points where the line y = x + 1 meets the circle x² + y² = 25.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the exact length of the chord joining these points.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Show that the line 3x + 4y = 25 is a tangent to the circle x² + y² = 25, and find the point of contact.
parts.answer: Substitution gives x² − 6x + 9 = 0, a repeated root; point of contact (3, 4)
parts.working: M1 substitute y = (25 − 3x)/4. A1 25x² − 150x + 225 = 0 → (x − 3)² = 0. A1 repeated root so tangent. A1 (3, 4).

parts.label: b
parts.text: Write down the equation of the tangent to the same circle at the point (−3, −4).

parts.label: a
parts.text: The circle (x − 2)² + (y − 3)² = 25 meets the x-axis at A and B. Find the coordinates of A and B.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the exact coordinates of the points where the circle meets the y-axis.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Find the area of the triangle formed by A, B and the centre of the circle.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the values of k for which the line y = kx is a tangent to the circle (x − 4)² + y² = 8.
parts.working: M1 substitute: (1 + k²)x² − 8x + 8 = 0. M1 discriminant: 64 − 32(1 + k²) = 0. A1 k² = 1. A1 k = ±1.

parts.label: b
parts.text: State the set of values of k for which the line meets the circle at two distinct points.

parts.label: c
parts.text: For k = 1, find the point of contact.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The line x + y = k meets the circle x² + y² − 4x − 2y − 20 = 0. Show that the x-coordinates of the points of intersection satisfy 2x² − (2k + 2)x + k² − 2k − 20 = 0.
parts.answer: Substituting y = k − x and simplifying gives 2x² − (2k + 2)x + (k² − 2k − 20) = 0
parts.working: M1 substitute y = k − x and expand. A1 correct simplification to the given equation.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the exact values of k for which the line is a tangent to the circle.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The line y = x − 1 meets the circle (x − 1)² + (y − 2)² = 10 at the points A and B. Find the coordinates of A and B.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the coordinates of the midpoint M of AB and show that CM is perpendicular to AB, where C is the centre of the circle.
parts.answer: M(2, 1); gradient CM = −1, gradient AB = 1, product −1
parts.working: B1 M(2, 1). B1 gradients −1 and 1 so perpendicular.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Find the exact perpendicular distance from C to the line AB.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The line y = x + c and the circle (x − 5)² + (y + 2)² = 18 are given. Show that the x-coordinates of any points of intersection satisfy 2x² + (2c − 6)x + c² + 4c + 11 = 0.
parts.working: M1 substitute and expand (x − 5)² + (x + c + 2)² = 18. A1 given equation.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the set of values of c for which the line does not meet the circle.
parts.working: M1 discriminant < 0: (2c − 6)² − 8(c² + 4c + 11) < 0. A1 −4c² − 56c − 52 < 0, i.e. c² + 14c + 13 > 0. M1 critical values −13, −1. A1 c < −13 or c > −1.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The line y = 2x + 5 meets the circle x² + y² − 2x − 4y − 20 = 0 at A and B. Find the coordinates of A and B.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the equation of the circle which has AB as a diameter.
parts.working: B1 centre (−1, 3). M1 r² = 2² + 4² = 20. A1 equation.

parts.label: c
parts.text: C is the centre of the original circle. Find the area of triangle ABC.
parts.working: M1 C(1, 2); e.g. ½|0 × (−3) − 5 × (−4)|, or base CA = 5 vertical with horizontal distance 4 to B. A1 10.

parts.label: a
parts.text: A circle has centre (3, −2) and radius 5. Write down the equation of the circle.
parts.working: B1 for (x − 3)² + (y + 2)² = 25 or the expanded form x² + y² − 6x + 4y − 12 = 0.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Determine whether the point (6, 2) lies on, inside or outside the circle.
parts.working: M1 substitute (6, 2) into the equation or find its distance from the centre. A1 25 = 25 (distance 5), so the point lies on the circle.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the coordinates of the centre and the radius of the circle with equation x² + y² − 8x + 6y − 11 = 0.
parts.working: M1 complete the square: (x − 4)² + (y + 3)² = 11 + 16 + 9. A1 centre (4, −3). A1 radius √36 = 6.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the exact distance from the origin to the centre, and hence state whether the origin lies inside or outside the circle.
parts.answer: Distance 5; 5 < 6 so the origin is inside the circle

parts.label: a
parts.text: The points A(−1, 4) and B(7, −2) are the ends of a diameter of a circle. Find the coordinates of the centre and the radius of the circle.
parts.working: B1 midpoint (3, 1). M1 AB = √(8² + 6²) = 10 or distance from centre to A. A1 radius 5.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the equation of the circle, giving your answer in the form x² + y² + ax + by + c = 0.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The points P(1, 1), Q(7, 1) and R(1, 9) lie on a circle. Show that angle QPR = 90° and explain why QR is a diameter of the circle.
parts.answer: PQ is horizontal and PR is vertical, so angle QPR = 90°; the angle in a semicircle is 90°, so QR is a diameter
parts.working: B1 PQ along y = 1 and PR along x = 1 (or gradients 0 and undefined), so perpendicular. B1 angle in a semicircle / converse, so QR is a diameter.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the equation of the circle.
parts.working: B1 centre = midpoint of QR = (4, 5). M1 radius = ½√(6² + 8²) = 5. A1 (x − 4)² + (y − 5)² = 25.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Find the equation of the tangent to the circle at R, giving your answer in the form ax + by + c = 0.
parts.working: M1 gradient of radius from (4, 5) to R(1, 9) = −4/3. M1 tangent gradient 3/4 through R. A1 3x − 4y + 33 = 0.

parts.label: a
parts.text: A circle passes through the points A(2, 0) and B(6, 4). Find the equation of the perpendicular bisector of AB.
parts.working: B1 midpoint (4, 2). B1 gradient AB = 1 so perpendicular gradient −1. A1 y − 2 = −(x − 4), i.e. y = 6 − x.

parts.label: b
parts.text: The centre of the circle lies on the line y = 2x − 3. Find the equation of the circle.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The circle C has equation x² + y² + 2x − 10y + k = 0, where k is a constant. The radius of C is 4. Find the value of k.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the exact y-coordinates of the points where C meets the y-axis.
parts.working: M1 x = 0: y² − 10y + 10 = 0. M1 formula or completing square: (y − 5)² = 15. A1 y = 5 ± √15.

parts.label: a
parts.text: A circle lies in the first quadrant and touches both the x-axis and the y-axis. Explain why its equation can be written as (x − r)² + (y − r)² = r², where r is the radius.
parts.answer: Touching both axes means the centre is a distance r from each axis, so the centre is (r, r)
parts.working: B1 centre at distance r from both axes, so (r, r).

parts.label: b
parts.text: The circle passes through the point (2, 1). Find the two possible equations of the circle.
parts.working: M1 (2 − r)² + (1 − r)² = r². A1 r² − 6r + 5 = 0. M1 r = 1 or r = 5. A1 both equations.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Find the distance between the centres of the two circles, giving your answer in exact form.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Circle C₁ has centre (1, 2) and radius 3. Circle C₂ has centre (7, 10) and radius 7. Show that the two circles touch externally.
parts.answer: Distance between centres = √(6² + 8²) = 10 = 3 + 7, so they touch externally
parts.working: M1 distance between centres √(36 + 64). A1 10. A1 equals sum of radii 3 + 7, so they touch (externally).

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the coordinates of the point where the circles touch.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Find the equation of the common tangent to the two circles at this point.
parts.working: M1 gradient of line of centres 4/3, so tangent gradient −3/4. A1 3x + 4y = 26.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The points A(−2, 5) and B(4, 1) are given. Find the equation of the perpendicular bisector of AB, giving your answer in the form ax + by + c = 0.
parts.working: B1 midpoint (1, 3). B1 gradient AB = −2/3. M1 perpendicular gradient 3/2 through midpoint. A1 3x − 2y + 3 = 0.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the equation of the line through (3, −1) that is parallel to the line 2x + 5y = 7.
parts.working: M1 gradient −2/5 (or same left-hand side). A1 2x + 5y = 1.

parts.label: b
parts.text: This line meets the x-axis at P and the y-axis at Q. Find the exact length PQ.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Triangle ABC has vertices A(1, 2), B(9, 6) and C(3, 8). Find the equation of AB.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the coordinates of the foot F of the perpendicular from C to AB.
parts.working: M1 line through C with gradient −2: y = −2x + 14. M1 solve with AB. A1 (5, 4).

parts.label: c
parts.text: Hence find the area of triangle ABC.

parts.label: a
parts.text: A(2, 1) and B(8, 5) are two points. The point C lies on the y-axis and is equidistant from A and B. Find the coordinates of C.
parts.working: M1 perpendicular bisector: midpoint (5, 3), gradient −3/2. A1 y − 3 = −3/2(x − 5). M1 x = 0. A1 y = 10.5. (Or M1 A1 using CA² = CB² with C(0, c).)

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the area of triangle ABC.
parts.working: M1 shoelace or ½ × base × height. A1 32.5.

parts.label: a
parts.text: ABCD is a rhombus. A is (−1, 2) and C is (7, 6). Find the equation of the diagonal BD.
parts.working: B1 midpoint of AC (3, 4). B1 gradient AC = ½, so BD gradient −2. A1 y = −2x + 10.

parts.label: b
parts.text: B lies on the x-axis. Find the coordinates of B and D.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Find the area of the rhombus and show that ABCD is in fact a square.
parts.answer: Area 40; AC = BD = √80 (diagonals equal and perpendicular), so it is a square
parts.working: M1 AC = √80, BD = √80. A1 area ½ × √80 × √80 = 40. A1 equal perpendicular bisecting diagonals ⇒ square.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The line l has equation y = 2x + 1. Find the coordinates of the foot of the perpendicular from P(6, 3) to l.
parts.working: M1 gradient −½ through P: y = −½x + 6. M1 solve 2x + 1 = −½x + 6. A1 (2, 5).

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the coordinates of the reflection of P in l, and the exact perpendicular distance from P to l.

practice.stem:
The random variable X has probability density function given by
f(x) = (3/8)x² for 0 ≤ x ≤ 2,
f(x) = 0 otherwise.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find E(X).

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find Var(X).

practice.stem:
The random variable X has probability density function given by
f(x) = x/8 for 0 ≤ x ≤ 4,
f(x) = 0 otherwise.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the median of X, giving your answer in exact form.
parts.working: M1 ∫₀^m x/8 dx = ½; A1 m²/16 = ½; A1 m = 2√2.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find E(X).

practice.stem:

f(x) = 0 otherwise.

parts.label: a

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the median of X, correct to 3 significant figures.

practice.stem:
The proportion X of a petrol tank that is empty when a car arrives at a filling station has probability density function
f(x) = 2(1 − x) for 0 ≤ x ≤ 1,
f(x) = 0 otherwise.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find E(X).

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the median of X, giving your answer in exact form.
parts.working: M1 2m − m² = ½; A1 2m² − 4m + 1 = 0; A1 m = 1 − 1/√2 (other root > 1).

practice.stem:
The time, X seconds, taken by a student to react to a signal in an experiment has probability density function
f(x) = 2/x² for 1 ≤ x ≤ 2,
f(x) = 0 otherwise.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the exact value of E(X).

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the median of X.

practice.stem:
The error, X mm, in the length of a machined part has probability density function
f(x) = (3/4)(1 − x²) for −1 ≤ x ≤ 1,
f(x) = 0 otherwise.

parts.label: a
parts.text: State the value of E(X), giving a reason.
parts.answer: 0, because the graph of f is symmetrical about x = 0

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find Var(X).

practice.stem:

f(x) = k/√x for 1 ≤ x ≤ 9,
f(x) = 0 otherwise.

parts.label: a

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find E(X).

parts.label: c

practice.stem:

f(t) = (10 − t)/50 for 0 ≤ t ≤ 10,
f(t) = 0 otherwise.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the mean waiting time.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the median waiting time, correct to 3 significant figures.

practice.stem:
The random variable X has probability density function given by
f(x) = 4x³ for 0 ≤ x ≤ 1,
f(x) = 0 otherwise.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find E(X) and Var(X).
parts.working: M1 ∫₀¹ 4x⁴ dx = 4/5; A1; M1 E(X²) = 4/6 and subtract (4/5)²; A1 2/75.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Hence find E(3X + 2) and Var(3X + 2).

parts.label: c
parts.text: Find the median of X, correct to 3 significant figures.

practice.stem:

f(x) = 0 otherwise.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Show that k = 12.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find P(X < ½).

parts.label: c

practice.stem:
The random variable X has probability density function given by

f(x) = 0 otherwise.

parts.label: a

parts.label: b

practice.stem:

parts.label: b

parts.label: c
parts.text: Show that the upper quartile q satisfies u³ − 12u + 8 = 0, where u = q − 3, and find q correct to 3 significant figures.

practice.stem:

f(x) = a + bx² for 0 ≤ x ≤ 1,
f(x) = 0 otherwise, where a and b are constants.

parts.label: a

parts.label: b

practice.stem:
The time, X hours after 2 pm, at which a power cut ends on a particular afternoon is modelled by the probability density function
f(x) = kx²(3 − x) for 0 ≤ x ≤ 3,
f(x) = 0 otherwise.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the value of k.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find E(X).

parts.label: c
parts.text: Show that the median of X lies between E(X) and 2.

practice.stem:
The random variable X has probability density function given by
f(x) = kx² for 0 ≤ x ≤ 3,
f(x) = 0 otherwise.

parts.label: a

parts.label: b

practice.stem:
The random variable X has probability density function given by
f(x) = k(4 − x) for 0 ≤ x ≤ 4,
f(x) = 0 otherwise.

parts.label: a

practice.stem:

parts.label: a

parts.working: M1 ∫₀² (a + bx) dx = 2a + 2b = 1; M1 ∫₀¹ (a + bx) dx = a + b/2 = 0.4; A1 both equations; M1 solve; A1 a = 0.3, b = 0.2.

parts.label: b

practice.stem:
The random variable X has probability density function given by
f(x) = k(1 + x)(3 − x) for 0 ≤ x ≤ 3,
f(x) = 0 otherwise.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the value of k.
parts.working: M1 expand (1 + x)(3 − x) = 3 + 2x − x²; M1 k[3x + x² − x³/3]₀³ = 9k; A1 9k = 1, k = 1/9.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find P(X > 2).

parts.label: a
parts.text: The variables x and y satisfy dy/dx = 6x²y, and y = 2 when x = 0. Solve the differential equation, obtaining an expression for y in terms of x.
parts.working: M1 separate: ∫(1/y) dy = ∫6x² dx. A1 ln y = 2x³ + c. M1 use x = 0, y = 2: c = ln 2. A1 y = 2e^(2x³).

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the value of y when x = 0.5, giving your answer correct to 3 significant figures.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Given that dy/dx = e^(2x − y) and y = 0 when x = 0, show that y = ln(½(e^(2x) + 1)).
parts.answer: eʸ = ½e^(2x) + ½, so y = ln(½(e^(2x) + 1))
parts.working: M1 write as eʸ dy/dx = e^(2x) and separate. A1 eʸ = ½e^(2x) + c. M1 use initial condition. A1 c = ½. A1 given answer correctly obtained.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the value of y when x = 1, giving your answer correct to 3 significant figures.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The variables x and y are related by 2y dy/dx = 3x² + 2, where y > 0, and y = 4 when x = 0. Find y² in terms of x.
parts.working: M1 ∫2y dy = ∫(3x² + 2) dx. A1 y² = x³ + 2x + c. A1 c = 16.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the exact value of y when x = 2.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Find the value of x for which y = 2√3, giving your answer correct to 3 significant figures.
parts.working: M1 x³ + 2x + 16 = 12, i.e. x³ + 2x + 4 = 0, solved numerically. A1 x = −1.18.

parts.label: a
parts.text: In a chemical reaction in a laboratory in Karachi, the mass x grams of product formed after t seconds satisfies dx/dt = 0.02(50 − x), and x = 0 when t = 0. Solve the differential equation to show that x = 50(1 − e^(−0.02t)).
parts.working: M1 ∫1/(50 − x) dx = ∫0.02 dt. A1 −ln(50 − x) = 0.02t + c. M1 c = −ln 50. A1 given answer.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the time taken for 40 grams of product to form, correct to 3 significant figures.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Solve the differential equation (x + 1) dy/dx = 2y, for x > −1 and y > 0, given that y = 5 when x = 0. Give y in terms of x.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the value of x for which y = 45.

parts.label: a
parts.text: After its engine is switched off, a boat on Keenjhar Lake slows so that its speed v m s⁻¹ after t seconds satisfies dv/dt = −0.02v². When t = 0, v = 10. Show that v = 50/(t + 5).
parts.working: M1 ∫v⁻² dv = −∫0.02 dt. A1 −1/v = −0.02t + c. M1 c = −0.1. A1 given answer.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the speed after 15 seconds and the time taken for the speed to fall to 4 m s⁻¹.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The variables x and y satisfy dy/dx = e^(x + y), and y = 0 when x = 0. Find y in terms of x.
parts.working: M1 ∫e^(−y) dy = ∫eˣ dx. A1 −e^(−y) = eˣ + c. M1 c = −2. A1 e^(−y) = 2 − eˣ. A1 y = −ln(2 − eˣ).

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find y when x = 0.5, correct to 3 significant figures, and state the exact value that x approaches as y tends to infinity.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The variables x and y satisfy cos² x dy/dx = √y, for 0 ≤ x < ½π, with y = 1 when x = 0. Find y in terms of x.
parts.working: M1 ∫y^(−½) dy = ∫sec² x dx. A1 2√y = tan x + c. M1 c = 2. A1 y = ¼(tan x + 2)².

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the exact value of y when x = π/4.

parts.label: a
parts.text: A cup of chai at 90 °C is left in a room at 25 °C. Its temperature θ °C after t minutes satisfies dθ/dt = −k(θ − 25), where k is a positive constant. Solve the differential equation to find θ in terms of k and t.

parts.label: b
parts.text: After 5 minutes the temperature is 60 °C. Find the value of k correct to 3 significant figures.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Find the temperature of the chai after 12 minutes, correct to the nearest degree.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The variables x and y satisfy dy/dx = y² sin x, and y = 0.5 when x = 0. Solve the differential equation, giving y in terms of x.
parts.working: M1 ∫y⁻² dy = ∫sin x dx. A1 −1/y = −cos x + c. M1 x = 0, y = 0.5: −2 = −1 + c. A1 c = −1. A1 y = 1/(1 + cos x).

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the exact value of y when x = π/3.

parts.label: c
parts.text: State what happens to y as x approaches π.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Given that dy/dx = x(1 + y²) and y = 1 when x = 0, show that y = tan(½x² + ¼π).
parts.answer: tan⁻¹ y = ½x² + π/4, so y = tan(½x² + π/4)
parts.working: M1 separate: ∫1/(1 + y²) dy = ∫x dx. A1 tan⁻¹ y. A1 ½x² + c. M1 c = tan⁻¹ 1 = π/4. A1 given answer.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the value of y when x = 0.8, giving your answer correct to 3 significant figures.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Find the exact positive value of x at which y becomes infinite for the first time.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The variables x and y satisfy y dy/dx = x e^(2x), with y = 1 when x = 0 and y > 0. Find y² in terms of x.
parts.working: M1 ∫y dy = ∫xe^(2x) dx. M1 integration by parts. A1 ½xe^(2x) − ¼e^(2x). A1 ½y² = ½xe^(2x) − ¼e^(2x) + c, c = ¾. A1 y² = xe^(2x) − ½e^(2x) + 3/2.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the value of y when x = 1, correct to 3 significant figures.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Solve the differential equation dy/dx = y ln x, for x > 0, given that y = 1 when x = 1. Give your answer in the form y = f(x).
parts.answer: y = e^(x ln x − x + 1) = xˣe^(1 − x)
parts.working: M1 ∫(1/y) dy = ∫ln x dx. M1 by parts: ∫ln x dx = x ln x − x. A1 ln y = x ln x − x + c. A1 c = 1. A1 y = e^(x ln x − x + 1).

parts.label: b
parts.text: Show that y = 27e⁻² when x = 3, and evaluate this correct to 3 significant figures.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The variables x and y satisfy dy/dx = (y + 2) cos 2x, and y = 1 when x = 0. Solve the differential equation, obtaining y in terms of x.
parts.working: M1 ∫1/(y + 2) dy = ∫cos 2x dx. A1 ln(y + 2). A1 ½ sin 2x + c. M1 c = ln 3. A1 y = 3e^(½ sin 2x) − 2.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the greatest value of y, correct to 3 significant figures, and the least positive value of x at which it occurs.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Water drains from a tank so that the depth h metres after t minutes satisfies dh/dt = −k√h, where k is a constant. Initially h = 4, and after 10 minutes h = 1. Show that 2√h = 4 − 0.2t.
parts.answer: 2√h = −kt + 4; using h = 1 at t = 10 gives k = 0.2, so 2√h = 4 − 0.2t
parts.working: M1 ∫h^(−½) dh = −∫k dt. A1 2√h = −kt + c. A1 c = 4. M1 substitute t = 10, h = 1. A1 k = 0.2 and given answer.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the depth after 5 minutes and the time at which the tank becomes empty.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Air is pumped into a weather balloon so that its volume V cm³ at time t seconds satisfies dV/dt = 300/√V. When t = 0, V = 100. Find an expression for V^(3/2) in terms of t.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the volume when t = 10, correct to 3 significant figures, and the time at which the volume reaches 400 cm³.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The variables θ and y satisfy dy/dθ = y sin² θ, and y = 2 when θ = 0. Solve the differential equation, obtaining y in terms of θ.
parts.working: M1 ∫(1/y) dy = ∫sin² θ dθ. M1 use sin² θ = ½(1 − cos 2θ). A1 ½θ − ¼ sin 2θ. A1 ln y = ½θ − ¼ sin 2θ + c. M1 c = ln 2. A1 answer.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the value of y when θ = π, correct to 3 significant figures.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The population P of goats on a farm in Balochistan at time t years is modelled by dP/dt = 0.1P − 20, and P = 300 when t = 0. Show that P = 200 + 100e^(0.1t).
parts.working: M1 ∫1/(0.1P − 20) dP = ∫dt. A1 10 ln(0.1P − 20) = t + c. M1 use t = 0, P = 300. A1 c = 10 ln 10. A1 rearrange to given answer.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the time taken for the population to double, correct to 3 significant figures.

parts.label: c
parts.text: State what would happen to the population if instead P = 200 when t = 0.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The number of fish, N, in a pond at time t months is modelled by dN/dt = 0.0005N(800 − N). When t = 0, N = 100. Using partial fractions, solve the differential equation to show that N = 800/(1 + 7e^(−0.4t)).
parts.working: M1 separate. M1 1/(N(800 − N)) = (1/800)(1/N + 1/(800 − N)). A1 (1/800)(ln N − ln(800 − N)) = 0.0005t + c. M1 use t = 0, N = 100. A1 ln(N/(800 − N)) = 0.4t + ln(1/7). A1 rearranged to the given form.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the number of fish after 5 months.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Find the time taken for the number of fish to reach 600, giving your answer correct to 3 significant figures, and state what happens to N in the long term.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The variables x and y satisfy x dy/dx = y² − 1, for x > 0, y > 1, and y = 3 when x = 1. Show that y = (2 + x²)/(2 − x²).
parts.answer: ½ ln((y − 1)/(y + 1)) = ln x + ½ ln ½, so (y − 1)/(y + 1) = ½x², giving y = (2 + x²)/(2 − x²)
parts.working: M1 separate: ∫1/(y² − 1) dy = ∫1/x dx. M1 partial fractions ½(1/(y − 1) − 1/(y + 1)). A1 ½ ln(y − 1) − ½ ln(y + 1). A1 = ln x + c. M1 c = ½ ln(1/2). M1 remove logs: (y − 1)/(y + 1) = ½x². A1 rearrange to given answer.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the value of y when x = 1.2, correct to 3 significant figures, and explain why the solution is valid only for x < √2.
parts.answer: y = 6.14; at x = √2 the denominator is zero (y → ∞)

parts.label: a
parts.text: Given that dy/dx = cos² y tan x, for 0 ≤ x < ½π, and y = 0 when x = 0, show that tan y = ln(sec x).
parts.answer: ∫sec² y dy = ∫tan x dx gives tan y = ln(sec x) + c with c = 0
parts.working: M1 separate: ∫sec² y dy = ∫tan x dx. A1 tan y. A1 −ln(cos x) or ln(sec x). M1 use y = 0, x = 0 to find c = 0. A1 given result.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the value of y when x = π/3, giving your answer in radians correct to 3 significant figures.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The variables x and y satisfy x(x + 1) dy/dx = 2y + 1, for x > 0, and y = 1.5 when x = 1. Show that 2y + 1 = 16x²/(x + 1)².
parts.answer: ½ ln(2y + 1) = ln x − ln(x + 1) + ln 4, so 2y + 1 = 16x²/(x + 1)²
parts.working: M1 separate: ∫1/(2y + 1) dy = ∫1/(x(x + 1)) dx. B1 1/(x(x + 1)) = 1/x − 1/(x + 1). A1 ½ ln(2y + 1). A1 ln x − ln(x + 1). M1 use x = 1, y = 1.5: ½ ln 4 = ln ½ + c. A1 c = ln 4. A1 given result.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find y in terms of x and state the limiting value of y as x becomes very large.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The variables x and y satisfy dy/dx = x(y + 1)²e^(−x), and y = 0 when x = 0. Show that 1/(y + 1) = (x + 1)e^(−x).
parts.working: M1 ∫(y + 1)⁻² dy = ∫xe^(−x) dx. A1 −1/(y + 1). M1 integration by parts. A1 −xe^(−x) − e^(−x). M1 use initial condition: c = 0. A1 given answer.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the value of y when x = 2, correct to 3 significant figures.

parts.label: a
parts.text: A news item spreads through a town. The number of people, x thousand, who have heard it t days after it was posted satisfies dx/dt = kx(5 − x), where k is a constant. When t = 0, x = 1 and when t = 1, x = 2. Show that ln(4x/(5 − x)) = 5kt and find the value of k correct to 3 significant figures.
parts.working: M1 separate and use partial fractions 1/(x(5 − x)) = (1/5)(1/x + 1/(5 − x)). A1 (1/5)(ln x − ln(5 − x)). A1 = kt + c. M1 t = 0, x = 1: c = (1/5) ln ¼. A1 given form. M1 t = 1, x = 2: ln(8/3) = 5k. A1 k = 0.196.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the number of people who have heard the item after 3 days, to the nearest hundred.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Given that (x + 1) dy/dx = y² + 4, for x > −1, and y = 2 when x = 0, show that y = 2 tan(2 ln(x + 1) + ¼π).
parts.answer: ½ tan⁻¹(y/2) = ln(x + 1) + π/8, so y = 2 tan(2 ln(x + 1) + π/4)
parts.working: M1 separate: ∫1/(y² + 4) dy = ∫1/(x + 1) dx. A1 ½ tan⁻¹(y/2). A1 ln(x + 1). M1 use y = 2, x = 0. A1 c = π/8. A1 given answer.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the value of y when x = 0.2, correct to 3 significant figures.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Given that dy/dx = 4 − y², with |y| < 2, and y = 0 when x = 0, show that y = 2(e^(4x) − 1)/(e^(4x) + 1).
parts.answer: (1/4) ln((2 + y)/(2 − y)) = x, so (2 + y)/(2 − y) = e^(4x), giving the result
parts.working: M1 separate. M1 partial fractions 1/(4 − y²) = (1/4)(1/(2 − y) + 1/(2 + y)). A1 (1/4)(ln(2 + y) − ln(2 − y)). A1 = x + c. B1 c = 0. M1 remove logarithms. A1 rearrange to the given answer.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the value of y when x = 0.25, correct to 3 significant figures, and state the limiting value of y as x → ∞.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The number of users P of a ride-hailing app in a city increases at a rate proportional to P. At a certain time, when P = 2000, P is increasing at 100 users per day. Write down a differential equation relating P and t (days) and find the constant of proportionality.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Taking t = 0 when P = 2000, solve the differential equation and find P when t = 10, to the nearest whole number.

parts.label: a
parts.text: A metal casting at a foundry in Gujranwala cools so that the rate of decrease of its temperature θ °C is proportional to the difference between θ and the surrounding temperature of 30 °C. Initially θ = 200 and the temperature is falling at 8.5 °C per minute. Form a differential equation and find the constant of proportionality.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Solve the differential equation and find the temperature after 20 minutes.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Find the time taken for the temperature to fall to 50 °C.

parts.label: a
parts.text: A container is filled with water. When the depth of water is h cm, the volume is V = 4h³ cm³. Water leaks out through a small hole at a rate of 2√h cm³ per second. Show that dh/dt = −1/(6h^(3/2)).
parts.working: B1 dV/dh = 12h². M1 chain rule dV/dt = (dV/dh)(dh/dt) with dV/dt = −2√h. A1 given answer.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Initially the depth is 16 cm. Solve the differential equation and find the time taken for the container to empty, giving your answer in minutes correct to 3 significant figures.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Gas escapes from a spherical balloon so that the rate of decrease of its volume is proportional to its radius r cm. Show that r dr/dt = −c, where c is a positive constant. [The volume of a sphere is (4/3)πr³.]
parts.working: B1 dV/dr = 4πr². M1 4πr² dr/dt = −kr. A1 r dr/dt = −c with c = k/(4π).

parts.label: b
parts.text: Initially r = 10, and after 6 seconds r = 8. Solve the differential equation to show that r² = 100 − 6t.
parts.working: M1 ∫r dr = −∫c dt. A1 ½r² = −ct + 50. A1 c = 3 and given answer.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Find the time at which the balloon has completely deflated, according to this model, correct to 3 significant figures.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The variables x and y satisfy y = Kxⁿ, where K and n are constants. The graph of ln y against ln x is a straight line passing through the points (0.5, 2.1) and (2.5, 0.9). Find the values of n and K, giving K correct to 3 significant figures.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The variables x and y satisfy y = A × bˣ, where A and b are constants. The graph of ln y against x is a straight line through (1, 3.2) and (4, 5.0). Find the values of A and b, correct to 3 significant figures.
parts.working: B1 ln y = ln A + x ln b; M1 gradient 1.8/3 = 0.6 = ln b; M1 intercept ln A = 3.2 − 0.6 = 2.6; A1 A = 13.5, b = 1.82.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The variables x and y satisfy y = axᵇ. The graph of ln y against ln x is a straight line with gradient 2.5 that crosses the vertical axis at 1.6. Find the values of a and b.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the value of y when x = 3, correct to 3 significant figures.

parts.label: a
parts.text: For the relationship y = A bˣ, state which graph should be drawn to give a straight line, and what its gradient represents.
parts.answer: ln y against x; gradient ln b
parts.working: B1 ln y against x; B1 gradient = ln b (intercept ln A).

parts.label: b
parts.text: The line obtained has equation ln y = 0.92 + 0.35x. Find A and b, correct to 3 significant figures.

practice.stem:
A laboratory culture of bacteria is counted every 2 hours. The number N of bacteria after t hours is modelled by N = N₀e^{kt}.
t (hours): 0, 2, 4, 6, 8
N: 250, 503, 1014, 2042, 4111

parts.label: a
parts.text: Show that the model N = N₀e^{kt} gives a straight line when ln N is plotted against t, and state what the gradient and intercept represent.
parts.answer: ln N = ln N₀ + kt; gradient k, intercept ln N₀
parts.working: M1 take ln of both sides; A1 gradient k, vertical intercept ln N₀.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Calculate the values of ln N for the table, correct to 2 decimal places, and use them to estimate k and N₀.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Use the model to estimate the number of bacteria after 10 hours, correct to 2 significant figures, and comment on the reliability of this estimate.
parts.answer: About 8300; it is an extrapolation beyond the data, so less reliable

practice.stem: A student in Lahore times a simple pendulum. The period T seconds and the length L metres are thought to satisfy T = kLⁿ. The graph of ln T against ln L is a straight line passing through the points (−1.20, 0.096) and (0.40, 0.896).

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the values of n and k, giving k correct to 3 significant figures.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Use your values to find the period of a pendulum of length 0.75 m, correct to 3 significant figures.

practice.stem: A cup of tea cools in a room at 20 °C. Its temperature θ °C after t minutes is modelled by θ − 20 = Ae^{−kt}. Readings: t = 0, θ = 80.0; t = 5, θ = 60.2; t = 10, θ = 47.0; t = 15, θ = 38.07.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Show that the model gives a straight line when ln(θ − 20) is plotted against t, stating the gradient and intercept in terms of A and k.
parts.answer: ln(θ − 20) = ln A − kt; gradient −k, intercept ln A

parts.label: b
parts.text: Use the readings at t = 0 and t = 15 to find the values of A and k, correct to 2 significant figures where necessary.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Find the time taken for the tea to cool to 30 °C, correct to 3 significant figures.

practice.stem: The population P million of a large city is modelled by P = a × bᵗ, where t is the number of years after the start of 2010. The graph of ln P against t is a straight line through (2, 2.65) and (10, 2.97).

parts.label: a

parts.label: b

parts.label: a
parts.text: The variables x and y satisfy y = Ae^{−kx²}. Explain why the graph of ln y against x² is a straight line.
parts.answer: ln y = ln A − kx², which is linear in x²

parts.label: b

parts.text: The variables x and y satisfy the equation y² = A bˣ, where A and b are constants. The graph of ln y against x is a straight line passing through (2, 1.45) and (5, 0.70). Find the values of A and b correct to 3 significant figures.
parts.working: B1 2 ln y = ln A + x ln b, so ln y = ½ ln A + (½ ln b)x; M1 gradient −0.75/3 = −0.25 = ½ ln b; A1 b = e^{−0.5} = 0.607; M1 intercept 1.45 + 0.5 = 1.95 = ½ ln A; A1 A = e^{3.9} = 49.4.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The variables x and y satisfy y = Axⁿ. When x = 2, y = 15 and when x = 5, y = 60. By taking natural logarithms, find the values of n and A correct to 3 significant figures.
parts.working: M1 ln 15 = ln A + n ln 2 and ln 60 = ln A + n ln 5; M1 subtract: ln 4 = n ln 2.5; A1 n = 1.51; M1 substitute back; A1 A = 15 ÷ 2^{1.513} = 5.26.

parts.label: b

parts.working: B1 gradient n = 1.51; B1 intercept ln A = 1.66.

parts.label: a

parts.working: M1 (x + 1) ln 5 = (2x − 1) ln 3; M1 collect x terms: x(2 ln 3 − ln 5) = ln 5 + ln 3; A1 x = ln 15/ln(9/5); A1 4.61.

parts.label: a

parts.working: M1 (3/2) log₃ x = 6; A1 log₃ x = 4, x = 81.

parts.text: A card is chosen at random from 20 cards numbered 1 to 20. A is the event 'the number is a multiple of 3', B is the event 'the number is even' and C is the event 'the number is greater than 15'. Find P(A | B) and hence show that A and B are independent.

parts.text: A factory in Sialkot makes footballs on three machines. Machine A makes 50% of the balls, B makes 30% and C makes 20%. The proportions of faulty balls are 2% from A, 3% from B and 5% from C. Find the probability that a randomly chosen ball is faulty.
